source.title: Discrete series multiplicities for classical groups over Z and level 1 algebraic cusp forms
readSections: The whole published article (63 pages, open-access PDF https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-020-00115-z.pdf, SHA-256 ea90fb0faabeaaa56be15f2c6f9c22450e7891c2181130fd79fe356cd83ba3de, accessed 2026-09-22), read in full from the text layer, with formulas, tables and every quoted passage checked on page images

Compared with arXiv 1907.08783v1 (20 Jul 2019, the only arXiv version; SHA-256 81b7fe2c31d0ab4ac7465c7d5209611638fa0d8c7c4ff11f7f4746866491742c): the published version adds Definition 5.3 (renumbering the later statements of §5) and the references [Kin03], [KSM04]; theorems, tables and numbers agree, and every source issue below is present in both

The authors' companion material [CT19b] from https://otaibi.perso.math.cnrs.fr/levelone/ (accessed 2026-09-22): readme.html (SHA-256 e86898d20f025e3cb415dc127ad5f371954e99754b640a1df8caac8cdf861012), mot23.pdf (562a1a471954c30733729d59c68bb389d6dbfcd1d8b4992657830269a7178b9f) and levelone_src_data.tar.gz (b0bd028b886b91d996d0562798c0800fdf465d7b39dc82eeea1a2e22ec6be87b): the mass tables, certificate lists, logs, PARI worksheets and the explicit-formula code, used to check Tables 2–3, Remark 3.10, the counts of Section 4 and the normalisation of β_Q

Mestre, Formules explicites et minorations de conducteurs de variétés algébriques, Compositio Math. 58 (1986), §§I.1–I.2 (Numdam PDF http://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1986__58_2_209_0.pdf, SHA-256 98150bde6477d77e4fc4983b4176562b62e7df69755446229c45cb7649bea024, accessed 2026-09-22), for the exact hypotheses of the explicit formula

The other cited inputs (Arthur, Chenevier–Lannes, Taïbi, Moeglin–Renard, Arancibia–Moeglin–Renard, Böcherer, Rallis and others) were not read; their statements are taken as the paper quotes them, and each item resting on one says so

summary: Chenevier and Taïbi turn Weil's explicit formula for the Rankin–Selberg L-functions of level one algebraic cusp forms into a positivity criterion on the cone spanned by Π_alg (Proposition 2.2 and Algorithms 2.4.4–2.4.5, certified in interval arithmetic). With it they (1) classify the level one algebraic cuspidal representations of PGL_m over Q of motivic weight 23 with the weight 23/2 of multiplicity one (Theorem 3) and the self-dual regular ones of motivic weight 24 (Theorem 5), and, under GRH, bound the rest of weight 23 (Theorem 4); (2) compute, by solving linear systems, the masses in the elliptic part of Arthur's L²-Lefschetz trace formula for SO_n (n ≤ 17) and Sp_2n (2n ≤ 16) (Theorems 6 and 7), after cutting down the conjugacy classes by spinor norms (Proposition 3.7); and (3) with Arthur's multiplicity formula and the Adams–Johnson and Moeglin–Renard packets, obtain dim S_k(Sp_2g(Z)) for g ≤ 8 and k_g > g (Theorem 1) and for all weights ≤ 13 (Theorem 2, Corollary 1), Eichler's basis problem for k = 4, 8, 12, the theta-series description of the four weight 13 forms, and results for g ≥ 2k (Corollaries 5.11, 5.14, 5.16, Proposition 5.15). The atlas plans Arthur's classification (ML.4), Rankin–Selberg L-functions (AL.3), the invariant trace formula (AS.6), the Satake transform (SR.4), algebraic weights (AF.4), lattice genera and theta series (GN.3, MP.5) and Siegel modular forms as sections of automorphic bundles (AutomorphicBundles B4); the libraries have Kronecker's theorem, cyclotomic polynomials and their values at 1, the archimedean Γ-factors, Mathlib's level one dimension formula for SL_2(Z), the Rayleigh-quotient eigenvector lemma and Tau Ceti's spinor norm over fields. Nothing plans level one automorphic forms of classical groups over Z, the explicit-formula classification method, the mass computation, or Siegel modular forms beyond their definition. These go to a new roadmap (LevelOneAutomorphicFormsForClassicalGroups), and 18 general inputs go as sources to 11 existing layers (AF.1, AL.1, AL.3, AN.3, AN.6, AS.6, ML.4, GN.2, MP.3, CN.4, CN.5). Eleven source issues are recorded, checked against the authors' published data and code: one error in the normalisation of Corollary 2.9 and Algorithm 2.4.5 (the element displayed in Section 4.1 has C(x, x) > 0), a gap in Proposition 4.1(1) (its U lies in the list V, so non-self-duality needs one more certificate, which the worker's uncertified run finds easily), a wrong dimension range for V, and eight misprints (Sp_14 has 1158 classes, not 1157; S_24 for S_23; inconsistent counts and set names in Section 4.1; δ = m = 2; Sp_2n for 2n ≤ 8; 15 for 16 elements; a page reference).

items.name: Split classical groups over Z
items.statement: A split classical group over Z is the group scheme Sp_2g over Z, or the special orthogonal group scheme SO_n of the quadratic form Σ_{i=1}^{n/2} x_i x_{n+1−i} (n even) or Σ_{i=1}^{(n−1)/2} x_i x_{n+1−i} + x_{(n+1)/2}^2 (n odd) on Z^n. Those of rank n form the families (SO_{2n+1})_{n≥1}, (Sp_{2n})_{n≥1} and (SO_{2n})_{n≥2}.
items.note: The libraries have the groups of R-points for every commutative ring R: Matrix.symplecticGroup (A J Aᵀ = J) and Tau Ceti's orthogonal and special orthogonal groups of a quadratic map over a commutative ring (read at f790474, OrthogonalGroup.lean:133 and :290). The paper uses only points over Z, Z_p, Q, Q_p, R, C and A; neither library has these groups as smooth affine group schemes over Z.

items.name: Which split classical groups have discrete series
items.statement: For G a split classical group over Z, G(R) has discrete series representations if and only if G is not isomorphic to SO_2n with n odd. The groups with discrete series are therefore (SO_{2n+1})_{n≥1}, (Sp_{2n})_{n≥1} and (SO_{4n})_{n≥1}.
items.note: Harish-Chandra's criterion (discrete series exist iff G(R) has a compact Cartan subgroup, i.e. rank G(R) = rank K) specialised to split classical groups. Stated without proof. No layer plans discrete series of real groups; routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1.

items.name: Level one
items.statement: A cuspidal automorphic representation π of PGL_m over Q has level 1 if π_p is unramified for every prime p.
items.note: AF.2 plans automorphic representations and their restricted tensor factorisation with almost-everywhere spherical vectors; SR.4 plans unramified representations and the Satake transform.

items.name: Algebraic cuspidal representations, weights and motivic weight
items.statement: A cuspidal automorphic representation π of PGL_m over Q is algebraic if the infinitesimal character of π_∞, viewed as a semisimple conjugacy class in M_m(C), has its eigenvalues in ½Z, say w_1 ≥ w_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ w_m, with w_i − w_j ∈ Z for all i, j. The w_i are the weights of π and w(π) := 2w_1 is its motivic weight.
items.note: AF.4 defines infinitesimal characters, algebraic weights and the C-algebraic and L-algebraic normalisations (Clozel). The symmetry w_{m+1−i} = −w_i is the item clozel-purity.

items.name: The sets W_m and regular weights
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, W_m is the set of w = (w_i) ∈ (½Z)^m with w_1 ≥ w_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ w_m, w_i − w_j ∈ Z and w_i = −w_{m+1−i} for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ m. An element w ∈ W_m is regular if for all i ≠ j either w_i ≠ w_j, or m ≡ 0 mod 4, i = j − 1 = m/2 and w_i = w_j = 0 (hence w_1 ∈ Z).

items.name: The counts N(w) and N⊥(w) (Problem 1)
items.statement: For w ∈ W_m, N(w) is the (finite) number of level 1 cuspidal algebraic automorphic representations of PGL_m over Q whose weights are the w_i, and N⊥(w) the number of those π with π^∨ ≃ π. Problem 1 asks to determine them.
items.note: Finiteness is Harish-Chandra's finiteness theorem; effective forms are corollary-2-3 (2.4.2) and chenevier-finiteness.

items.name: The set Π_alg
items.statement: Π_alg is the set of cuspidal automorphic representations of PGL_m over Q, with m ≥ 1 arbitrary, which are algebraic and of level 1. R Π_alg is the real vector space with basis Π_alg; for π ∈ Π_alg, sd(π) = 1 if π is self-dual and sd(π) = 0 otherwise.
items.locator: Section 1.3, p. 265; Section 2.1, p. 273; Section 2.3, p. 275; Section 2.4.2, p. 278

items.name: Key fact 1
items.statement: Fix g ≥ 1 and k = (k_1, …, k_g) ∈ Z^g with k_1 ≥ k_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g > g. Then dim S_k(Γ_g) is an explicit function of the finitely many quantities N⊥(w) with w = (w_i) ∈ W_m regular, m ≤ 2g + 1 and w_1 ≤ k_1 − 1.
items.locator: Section 1.2, Key fact 1, p. 265; made precise in Section 5.2.1
items.note: Recalled from [CR15, Chap. 9], [CR15, Prop. 1.11] (g ≤ 3), [Taï17, Chap. 5] (g = 4), [CL19, Thm. 5.2] (general recipe). The precise form is vector-valued-packet together with multiplicity-formula.

items.name: Classification in motivic weight ≤ 22 (Chenevier–Lannes)
items.statement: There are exactly 11 elements of Π_alg of motivic weight ≤ 22: the trivial representation of PGL_1; the 5 representations Δ_{k−1} of PGL_2 generated by the one-dimensional spaces S_k(SL_2(Z)) for k = 12, 16, 18, 20, 22 (weights ±(k−1)/2); the Gelbart–Jacquet symmetric square Sym²Δ_11 (weights −11, 0, 11); and four self-dual representations of PGL_4 with weights {±19/2, ±7/2}, {±21/2, ±5/2}, {±21/2, ±9/2} and {±21/2, ±13/2} (denoted Δ_{19,7}, Δ_{21,5}, Δ_{21,9}, Δ_{21,13}).
items.locator: Section 1.3, p. 265 ([CL19, Thm. F] = [CL19, Thm. 9.3.3]); new proof in Section 2.4.6
items.note: The paper reproves the hardest case (motivic weight 22) by Algorithm 2.4.5 without Satake parameters: item reproof-weight-22. The existence of the four PGL_4 forms comes from [CL19]/[CR15]; the paper reproves existence by the mass computation of Section 3 (item twenty-seven-known).

items.name: Theorem 3 (motivic weight 23, weight 23/2 of multiplicity one)
items.statement: There are exactly 13 level 1 cuspidal algebraic automorphic representations of PGL_m over Q, with m varying, with motivic weight 23 and having the weight 23/2 with multiplicity 1: (i) 2 representations of PGL_2 generated by the eigenforms in S_24(SL_2(Z)); (ii) 3 representations of PGL_4 of weights ±23/2, ±v/2 with v = 7, 9 or 13; (iii) 7 representations of PGL_6 of weights ±23/2, ±v/2, ±u/2 with (v, u) = (13, 5), (15, 3), (15, 7), (17, 5), (17, 9), (19, 3) and (19, 11); (iv) 1 representation of PGL_10 of weights ±23/2, ±21/2, ±17/2, ±11/2, ±3/2. They are all self-dual (symplectic) and uniquely determined by their weights.
items.locator: Section 1.3, Theorem 3, pp. 265–266; proof in Section 4.1, pp. 295–297
items.note: Proof: Fincke–Pohst lists U_1 (all effective U ∈ K_∞^{≤23} containing I_23 with B_∞(U,U) ≤ F̂(i/4π), ℓ = 9.74) and U_2 (bound F̂(i/4π)/2); Algorithm 2.4.5 with δ = 0, m = 2 on U_2 and with δ = m = 1 on U_1; the six multiplicity-free survivors are excluded by Section 3; the 181 others contain I_23 twice. Existence: Section 3.3. The counts in this proof carry source issues E4 and E5.

items.name: Theorem 4 (conditional on GRH)
items.statement: Assume (GRH) and that there exists a level 1 cuspidal algebraic automorphic representation π of PGL_m over Q having motivic weight 23 and having the weight 23/2 with multiplicity > 1. Then m = 16, the weights of π are ±1/2, ±7/2, ±11/2, ±15/2, ±19/2, ±21/2 as well as ±23/2 with multiplicity 2, and π is the unique element of Π_alg having these 16 weights.
items.locator: Section 1.3, Theorem 4, p. 266; proof in Section 4.3, p. 299
items.note: Proof uses the functions G_ℓ (Proposition 4.4): Algorithm 2.4.5 with m = 2 on the U of Proposition 4.1(1) (printed 'δ = m = 2'; source issue E8), then δ = m = 1 on each element of the list V. The remaining case A = I_1 + I_7 + I_11 + I_15 + I_19 + I_21 + 2I_23 is the one of the statement.

items.name: Theorem 5 (motivic weight 24, regular)
items.statement: There are exactly 3 level 1 algebraic cuspidal self-dual automorphic representations of PGL_m over Q, with m varying, with motivic weight 24 and regular weights. Their sets of weights are {±12, ±8, ±4, 0}, {±12, ±9, ±5, ±2} and {±12, ±10, ±7, ±1}.
items.locator: Section 1.3, Theorem 5, p. 266; proof in Section 4.2, p. 298
items.note: Denoted O^o_{24,16,8}, O^e_{24,18,10,4}, O^e_{24,20,14,2}. Proof: Lemma 4.3 bounds the dimension by 16; Theorem 6 then computes N⊥ for every multiplicity-free U ∈ K_∞^{≤24} containing I_24 with dim U ≤ 16. That needs SO_n for n ≤ 16 and Sp_2n for 2n ≤ 14 (printed '2n ≤ 8'; source issue E9).

items.name: Finiteness in motivic weight ≤ 23 (Chenevier)
items.statement: There are only finitely many level 1 cuspidal algebraic automorphic representations of PGL_m over Q, with m varying, of motivic weight ≤ 23; this also holds in motivic weight ≤ 24 assuming a suitable form of GRH. The result is effective (it leads to 12295 possible weights in motivic weight 23).
items.note: Cited from [Chea] (Chenevier, An automorphic generalization of the Hermite–Minkowski theorem). Not read. The proofs here use its engine directly: b-infinity-positive-definite and corollary-2-3.

items.name: Euler–Poincaré characteristic EP(G; λ)
items.statement: Let G be a split classical group over Z with discrete series, K a maximal compact subgroup of G(R), A²(G) the space of K-finite square-integrable automorphic forms on G(Z)\G(R), and V_λ an irreducible representation of G(C) of highest weight λ. Then EP(G; λ) = Σ_{i≥0} (−1)^i dim H^i(g, K; A²(G) ⊗ V_λ^∨) ∈ Z, with H^*(g, K; −) relative Lie algebra cohomology.
items.note: AF.1 plans relative Lie algebra cochains and AF.2 the automorphic spaces; the level-one L² Euler–Poincaré characteristic is new here.

items.name: The integer n_Ĝ and the weight w(λ)
items.statement: n_Ĝ is the dimension of the standard representation of the Langlands dual group Ĝ: n_Ĝ = 2n + 1 for G = Sp_2n and n_Ĝ = 2n for G = SO_{2n+1} or SO_2n. For a dominant weight λ = Σ λ_i e_i (λ_i ∈ Z, λ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_n, and λ_n ≥ 0 for Sp_2n and SO_{2n+1}, |λ_n| ≤ λ_{n−1} for SO_2n), the infinitesimal character λ + ρ of V_λ defines the regular element w(λ) ∈ W_{n_Ĝ} with w(λ)_i = λ_i + n + 1/2 − i (SO_{2n+1}), λ_i + n + 1 − i (Sp_2n), |λ_i| + n − i (SO_2n, n even), for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.

items.name: Every regular weight comes from a unique group
items.statement: Every regular w ∈ W_m, m ≥ 1, is of the form w(λ) for a unique split classical group G over Z (with G(R) having discrete series) and a dominant weight λ of G.

items.name: Key fact 2
items.statement: Fix G and λ as above and set w = w(λ). Assume N⊥(v) is known for all regular v ∈ W_m with m < n_Ĝ and v_1 ≤ w_1. Then it is equivalent to know EP(G; λ) or N⊥(w).
items.note: The explicit relation is not reproduced in the paper; it is [Taï17, §4], resting on Arthur's classification (ML.4) and the Adams–Johnson packets of [AJ87, AMR18] (item amr18-adams-johnson). Implemented in the authors' combi_endo.sage.

items.name: Arthur's L²-Lefschetz trace formula for level one
items.statement: Fix a Haar measure dg = Π'_v dg_v on G(A) with vol(G(Z_p)) = 1 for every p, and a dominant weight λ. For the test function φ = φ_∞ ⊗'_p 1_{G(Z_p)}, where φ_∞(g_∞)dg_∞ is the sum over the discrete series δ of G(R) with the infinitesimal character of V_λ of a pseudocoefficient of δ, Arthur's trace formula gives EP(G; λ) = T_geom(G; λ) (1.4.1). T_geom(G; λ) is a finite sum of terms indexed by Levi subgroups GL_1^a × GL_2^b × G′ (G′ split classical over Z, a, b ≥ 0), whose term for G itself is the elliptic term T_ell(G; λ) = Σ_γ vol(G_γ(Q)\G_γ(A)) · O_γ(1_{G(Ẑ)}) · tr(γ | V_λ) (1.4.3), γ running over the finitely many G(Q)-classes of finite-order elements of G(Q) whose G(Q_p)-class meets G(Z_p) for all p, with dh_∞ an Euler–Poincaré measure on G_γ(R) and O_γ the product of the local orbital integrals ∫_{G(Q_p)/G_γ(Q_p)} 1_{G(Z_p)}(g_p γ g_p^{−1}) dg_p/dh_p (1.4.4).
items.note: AS.6 plans Arthur's invariant trace formula; the L²-Lefschetz specialisation [Art89] (pseudocoefficients of discrete series, the simple geometric side) is not planned. ET.1 plans pseudocoefficients only in unitary cases. Routed to AS.6 as a source; [Art89] is a prerequisite.

items.name: Conjugacy classes C(G) and masses m_c
items.statement: C(G) is the set of G(Q̄)-conjugacy classes of finite-order elements of G(Q). Writing T_ell(G; λ) = Σ_{c ∈ C(G)} m_c tr(c | V_λ) (1.4.5) defines the mass m_c of c, a concrete sum of volumes times adelic orbital integrals depending only on c. If no element γ of c has a G(Q)-class meeting G(Z_p) for every p and a centraliser G_γ with G_γ(R) having discrete series, then m_c = 0 (Remark 1.1).

items.name: Masses are rational
items.statement: For every c ∈ C(G), m_c ∈ Q.
items.note: 'It essentially follows from [Gro97, Thm. 9.9] and Siegel's theorem on the rationality of the values of Artin L-functions at non-positive integers [Sie69]'. Stated without further proof.

items.name: Non-elliptic terms
items.statement: The term of T_geom(G; λ) attached to a proper Levi subgroup GL_1^a × GL_2^b × G′ is expressed in terms of T_ell(G′; λ′), as well as T_ell(SO_3; λ″) if b ≠ 0, for suitable auxiliary λ′, λ″.
items.note: The concrete formulas are in [Taï17, §3.3.4] (not reproduced); implemented in combi_Levi.sage.

items.name: Evaluating tr(c | V_λ)
items.statement: tr(c | V_λ) is well defined on C(G) and can be computed by the (degenerate) Weyl character formula [CR15] or, more efficiently for small λ, by Koike–Terada's formulas [KT87] for the irreducible representations of symplectic and orthogonal groups; the latter give tr(P; λ) in terms of the characteristic polynomial P.
items.note: The Weyl character formula is planned in Tau Ceti's Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas, Layer 6; its evaluation at torsion elements of G(C) and Koike–Terada's formulas are not.

items.name: The inductive strategy
items.statement: Suppose the masses m_c are known for every split classical H over Z with discrete series and n_Ĥ < m, and all c ∈ C(H), so that N⊥(w) is computable for every regular w ∈ W_{m′}, m′ < m. Let G have discrete series and n_Ĝ = m, and let Λ be a finite set of dominant weights with (P1) N⊥(w(λ)) = 0 for all λ ∈ Λ and (P2) the Λ × C(G) matrix (tr(c | V_λ)) has rank |C(G)|. Then the masses m_c, c ∈ C(G), are the unique solution of the linear system given by (1.4.1), Key fact 2 and (1.4.5), and EP(G; λ) and N⊥(w(λ)) are then computable for every dominant λ.

items.name: The example G = SO_3
items.statement: C(SO_3) has 5 classes c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4, c_6 (c_i of order i). For k ≥ 0, w(k) = (k + 1/2, −k − 1/2), N(w(k)) = dim S_{2k+2}(SL_2(Z)), EP(SO_3; k) = −N(w(k)) + δ_{k,0} and T_geom(SO_3; k) = T_ell(SO_3; k) + 1/2. With dim V_k = 2k + 1, tr(c_i | V_k) = sin((2k+1)π/i)/sin(π/i) for i > 1, Λ = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} and the vanishing of S_2, S_4, S_6, S_8, S_10, the linear system has the unique solution m_{c_1} = −1/12, m_{c_2} = 1/4, m_{c_3} = 1/3, m_{c_4} = m_{c_6} = 0, which gives the classical formula for dim S_2k(SL_2(Z)).
items.note: Checked by the worker: the 5×5 matrix [[1,1,1,1,1],[3,−1,0,1,2],[5,1,−1,−1,1],[7,−1,1,−1,−1],[9,1,0,1,−2]] is invertible, the stated masses solve it with right-hand side (1/2, −1/2, −1/2, −1/2, −1/2), and they reproduce dim S_{2k+2}(SL_2(Z)) for k < 40. Mathlib has the level-one dimension formula for even weight (ModularForm.dimension_level_one, read at 082e2d3).

items.name: Theorem 6 ('effortless' masses)
items.statement: Assume G = SO_n with n ≤ 17, or G = Sp_2n with 2n ≤ 14. Then the masses m_c, for all c ∈ C(G), are given in [CT19b].
items.locator: Section 1.4, Theorem 6, p. 272; proof in Section 3.3, pp. 292–294
items.note: Consequences: EP(G; λ) for all these G and all λ, and N⊥(w) for every w ∈ W_m, m ≤ 16. The published mass files agree with Remark 3.10 and Tables 2–3 (worker's check). The data are certificates (item certificates).

items.name: Theorem 7 (masses of Sp_16)
items.statement: The masses m_c, for all c ∈ C(Sp_16), are given in [CT19b].
items.locator: Section 1.4, Theorem 7, p. 272; proof in Section 3.3, pp. 294–295
items.note: Combines the method with direct orbital-integral computations of [Taï17] for P(Sp_16)^easy (item sp16-easy-hard).

items.name: Elliptic terms are indexed by finite-order classes
items.statement: The semisimple γ ∈ G(Q) contributing to T_ell(G; λ) are R-elliptic and their G(A_f)-class meets G(Ẑ); hence the characteristic polynomial P_γ lies in Z[X] and all its complex roots have absolute value 1, so they are roots of unity (Kronecker) and γ has finite order.
items.note: The Kronecker step is item kronecker.

items.name: Kronecker's theorem
items.statement: An algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have absolute value 1 is a root of unity.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3 (InfinitePlace/Embeddings.lean:138): for x in a number field K with IsIntegral ℤ x and ‖φ x‖ = 1 for every embedding φ into an algebraically closed normed field, some positive power of x is 1.

items.name: Definition 3.1: the set P(G)
items.statement: For G one of SO_{2n+1}, Sp_2n, SO_4n, let n_G = 2n + 1, 2n, 4n be the dimension of its standard representation. P(G) is the set of P ∈ Q[X] of degree n_G which are products of cyclotomic polynomials and in which X + 1 has even multiplicity (equivalently, P(0) = (−1)^{n_G}).

items.name: The characteristic-polynomial map
items.statement: The map char: C(G) → P(G), c ↦ P_c, is well defined. Two semisimple conjugacy classes of G(Q) with the same characteristic polynomial P are equal except when G = SO_4n, P(−1)P(1) ≠ 0 and they are conjugate under O_4n(Q)/SO_4n(Q) ≃ Z/2Z; so char^{−1}(P) has at most one element if G ≠ SO_4n or P(−1)P(1) = 0, and 0 or 2 elements otherwise. char is not surjective in general (for p ≡ 1 mod 4 prime there is no element of order p in SO_{p−1}(Q)).
items.note: 'It is well-known'; stated without proof. Footnote 11 uses Corollary 3.6.

items.name: Lemma 3.2
items.statement: For G = SO_4n and c, c′ ∈ C(G) with P_c = P_c′, m_c = m_c′. Hence T_ell(G; λ) = Σ_{P ∈ P(G)} m_P tr(P; λ) with m_P = m_c for any c with char(c) = P (0 if P ∉ char(C(G))), and tr(P; λ) = tr(c | V_λ) if G ≠ SO_4n or P(1)P(−1) = 0, tr(c | V_λ) + tr(c′ | V_λ) otherwise. In particular T_ell(SO_4n; θ(λ)) = T_ell(SO_4n; λ) for the outer automorphism θ induced by O_4n(Z)/SO_4n(Z).

items.name: Lemma 3.3
items.statement: For G = SO_4n or Sp_2n and c ∈ C(G), m_{−c} = m_c.
items.note: Formula (1.4.4) and centrality of −1 ∈ G(Z). Consistent with the published mass files (worker's check).

items.name: The reduced elliptic term (3.1.2)
items.statement: Define P_1 ∼ P_2 on P(G) if P_1 = P_2 or P_2(X) = (−1)^{n_G} P_1(−X), and let e_P ∈ {1, 2} be the size of the class of P. For G = SO_4n or Sp_2n, P_{−c}(X) = (−1)^{deg P_c} P_c(−X) and tr(P_{−c}; λ) = λ(−1) tr(P_c; λ), so T_ell(G; λ) = 0 if λ is non-trivial on the centre Z(G), and if λ|_{Z(G)} = 1 then T_ell(G; λ) = Σ_{P ∈ P(G)/∼} e_P m_P tr(P; λ).

items.name: Regular quadratic forms and discriminants over rings
items.statement: For R a commutative ring and V a projective R-module of constant rank n with a quadratic form q, q is non-degenerate if β_q(x, y) = q(x + y) − q(x) − q(y) is a perfect pairing, and regular if it is non-degenerate or n is odd and Zariski-locally the half-discriminant is invertible ([Knu91, IV §3], 'semi-regular'). For V free and q non-degenerate, disc(q) ∈ R^×/R^{×2} is the class of the determinant of a Gram matrix of β_q.
items.note: Mathlib has non-degeneracy and the discriminant of a form on ι → R; the odd-rank half-discriminant regularity over rings is missing.

items.name: GSpin, Spin and the spinor norm over rings
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and (V, q) regular over R: GSpin(V, q) is the group of even invertible elements of the Clifford algebra C(V, q) stabilising V under conjugation, with π: GSpin(V, q) → SO(V, q) of kernel the central GL_1 and Clifford norm ν: GSpin → GL_1 (ν(t) = t² on GL_1); Spin(V, q) = ker ν. There are exact sequences 1 → GL_1 → GSpin(V, q) → SO(V, q) → 1 of Zariski sheaves (3.2.1) and 1 → μ_2 → Spin(V, q) → SO(V, q) → 1 of fppf sheaves; the latter gives the spinor norm sn: SO(V, q)(R) → H¹_fppf(R, μ_2) ≃ R^×/R^{×2} when Pic R = 1, represented by ν(γ̃) for any lift γ̃ ∈ GSpin(V, q)(R). The spinor norm is multiplicative on orthogonal sums.
items.note: Mathlib has the Clifford algebra and its Lipschitz, Pin and Spin subgroups over a commutative ring; Tau Ceti has the spinor norm over a field (item spinor-norm-field). The group schemes over rings, the fppf sequence and the ring-valued spinor norm are missing.

items.name: The spinor norm over a field
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic ≠ 2 and a non-degenerate quadratic form q on a finite-dimensional k-vector space, the spinor norm sn: SO(V, q)(k) → k^×/k^{×2}, represented by the Clifford norm of a lift to GSpin; its kernel is the image of Spin(V, q)(k).
items.note: Read at f790474 (Spin/SpinorNorm/Basic.lean:143, :213, :323): over a field K with 2 invertible and Q non-degenerate, spinorNorm : SO(Q) →* SquareClassGroup K is the descended Clifford norm of Lipschitz lifts, and the image of Spin is its kernel.

items.name: Theorem 3.5 (Zassenhaus)
items.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic different from 2, V a finite-dimensional k-vector space with a non-degenerate quadratic form q, and γ ∈ SO(V, q)(k) with characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^a (X + 1)^{2b} Q(X), Q(1)Q(−1) ≠ 0. Then sn(γ) is represented by disc(q | ker(γ + 1)^{2b}) · Q(−1) in k^×/k^{×2}.
items.note: The paper gives a short proof (orthogonal decomposition, sn(−id_V) = 2^{dim V} disc(q), and a computation in the graded tensor product of Clifford algebras of hyperbolic planes).

items.name: Corollary 3.6
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 3.5 with a = b = 0, disc(q) ∈ k^×/k^{×2} is represented by Q(1)Q(−1).

items.name: Proposition 3.7
items.statement: Let V be a free Z-module of rank n with a regular quadratic form q, G = SO(V, q), and P(X) = (X − 1)^a (X + 1)^{2b} Q(X) monic of degree n in Q[X] with Q(1)Q(−1) ≠ 0. If for every prime p there is γ_p ∈ G(Z_p) with characteristic polynomial P, then |Q(−1)| is a square if b = 0, and |Q(1)| is a square if a = 0.
items.note: Similar to [GM02, Thm. 6.1] (Gross–McMullen); proof via lifting γ_p to GSpin(V, q)(Z_p) and Theorem 3.5.

items.name: Definition 3.8: the set P_1(G)
items.statement: For G = SO_{2n+1} or SO_4n, P_1(G) is the set of P ∈ P(G) of the form (X − 1)^a (X + 1)^{2b} Q(X), Q a product of cyclotomic polynomials Φ_m with m ≥ 3, such that b > 0 if the positive integer Q(−1) is not a square and a > 0 if the positive integer Q(1) is not a square. For G = Sp_2n, P_1(G) = P(G). P_1(G) is stable under ∼.

items.name: Values of cyclotomic polynomials at 1
items.statement: For m ≥ 2, Φ_m(1) = p if m = p^k is a power of a prime p (k ≥ 1), and Φ_m(1) = 1 otherwise; the values Φ_m(±1), m ≥ 3, are computed from the prime decomposition of m ([GM02, Thm. 7.1]).
items.note: Read at 082e2d3 (Cyclotomic/Eval.lean:42, :137). Φ_m(−1) follows from Φ_m(1) through Φ_m(−X) = Φ_{2m}(X) (m odd, m > 1), which is not stated in Mathlib in this form.

items.name: Corollary 3.9
items.statement: If P ∈ P(G) satisfies m_P ≠ 0, then P ∈ P_1(G).
items.note: From Proposition 3.7 and Remark 1.1. For Sp_2n one can show C_0(Sp_2n) = C(Sp_2n) (details left to the reader, [Taï17, §3.2.2], [Jac40]); this is not used.

items.name: The easy and hard classes of Sp_16
items.statement: For P ∈ P(Sp_16) and p prime write P = Π_{m} Π_{k ∈ S(p,m)} Φ_{m p^k}^{d(p,m,k)} (m prime to p, d ≥ 1). P ∈ P(Sp_16)^easy iff for every p and m, |S(p, m)| ≤ 2, with 0 ∈ S(p, m) if p > 2 and |S(p, m)| = 2, and 0 or 1 ∈ S(p, m) if p = 2 and |S(p, m)| = 2. For such P the orbital integrals in m_P are computed combinatorially by the method of [Taï17]. |P(Sp_16)^hard/∼| = 766, and there is Λ ⊂ Λ_G(36) of cardinality 1086 satisfying (P1′) and the analogue of (P2′) for P(Sp_16)^hard; the Sp_16 subset found by Algorithm 2.4.5 alone (in Λ_G(116)) has only 1427 elements against |P_1(Sp_16)/∼| = 2521.
items.note: The orbital-integral method of [Taï17] is not reproduced (Wall's invariants [Wal63] are avoided for easy P).

items.name: Local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(R)
items.statement: There is a natural bijection V ↦ L(V) between isomorphism classes of irreducible admissible Harish-Chandra modules for GL_n(R) and isomorphism classes of n-dimensional complex continuous semisimple representations of the Weil group W_R = C^× ∐ jC^× (j² = −1, jzj^{−1} = z̄).
items.note: Langlands' archimedean correspondence; not planned. Routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1.

items.name: Algebraic Harish-Chandra modules and the ring K_∞
items.statement: A Harish-Chandra module V for GL_n(R) is algebraic if every element of the centre R^× of W_R acts on L(V) by ±1; then L(V) factors through W_R/R_{>0}. Let 1 be the trivial representation, ε_{C/R} the order-2 character, and I_w = Ind_{C^×}^{W_R} η^w (η(z) = z/|z|); the irreducible representations of W_R trivial on R_{>0} are 1, ε_{C/R} and I_w (w > 0), with I_0 ≃ 1 ⊕ ε_{C/R} and I_w ≃ I_{w′} iff w = ±w′. K_∞ is the Grothendieck ring of these representations, with I_w·I_{w′} = I_{|w+w′|} + I_{|w−w′|} and ε_{C/R}·I_w = I_w; K_∞^{≤w} is the subgroup generated by the I_v with 0 ≤ v ≤ w, v ≡ w mod 2 (and 1, ε_{C/R} for w even). U ∈ K_∞ is effective if it is the class of a representation; its weights are the v/2 with η^v in U|_{C^×}, counted with multiplicity.

items.name: Purity and parameters of π ∈ Π_alg
items.statement: For π a cuspidal automorphic representation of PGL_n over Q, π_∞ is algebraic in the Harish-Chandra sense iff π is algebraic; the multiplicity of the weight v/2 of π equals that of η^v in L(π_∞)|_{C^×}. For π ∈ Π_alg, L(π_∞) ∈ K_∞^{≤w} for some w ≥ 0, the least such w is w(π), and the weights of π are those of L(π_∞); moreover w_{m+1−i} = −w_i (Jacquet–Shalika), so w(π) ≥ 0.
items.note: Clozel's purity lemma or the archimedean Jacquet–Shalika estimates; cited, not proved.

items.name: Archimedean Γ-factors
items.statement: Γ(s, U) is additive in U ∈ K_∞, with Γ(s, 1) = π^{−s/2} Γ(s/2) and Γ(s, I_w) = 2(2π)^{−s−|w|/2} Γ(s + |w|/2) for all w ∈ Z ([Tat79]).
items.note: Read at 082e2d3 (Gamma/Deligne.lean:45, :53): Gammaℝ s = π^{−s/2} Γ(s/2) and Gammaℂ s = 2(2π)^{−s} Γ(s), so Γ(s, 1) = Gammaℝ s and Γ(s, I_w) = Gammaℂ(s + |w|/2). Γ(s, ε_{C/R}) = Gammaℝ(s + 1), not stated in the paper, is consistent with I_0 = 1 + ε_{C/R} by Gammaℝ_mul_Gammaℝ_add_one (Gammaℝ s · Gammaℝ (s + 1) = Gammaℂ s).

items.name: Archimedean ε-factors
items.statement: ε(U) ∈ {±1, ±i} is additive in U ∈ K_∞, with ε(1) = 1 and ε(I_w) = i^{w+1} for every integer w ≥ 0; ε(U) is Tate's ε(U, ψ, dx) with ψ(x) = e^{2iπx} and dx the Lebesgue measure.
items.note: AL.1 plans Tate's local ε-factors for GL_1; the ε-factors of W_R-representations (by additivity and induction) are routed there.

items.name: Regular elements of Π_alg
items.statement: π ∈ Π_alg (on PGL_n) is regular if L(π_∞) is multiplicity free. (a) If all non-zero weights of π have multiplicity 1 and 0 has multiplicity 2, then π is regular iff n ≡ 0 mod 4. (b) π is regular iff its weight vector is regular in the sense of W_n. (c) If π is regular and n = 2g + 1 is odd, then L(π_∞) contains ε_{C/R}^g (as det L(π_∞) = 1 and det I_v = ε_{C/R}^{v+1}).

items.name: Symplectic and orthogonal self-dual representations
items.statement: A self-dual cuspidal π of PGL_n over Q is either symplectic or orthogonal in the sense of Arthur [Art13, Thm. 1.4.1], and if π is symplectic (resp. orthogonal) then L(π_∞) preserves a non-degenerate alternating (resp. symmetric) pairing [Art13, Thm. 1.4.2].
items.note: ML.4 gives the Arthur/Mok classification inputs explicit proof-source owners.

items.name: Type and motivic weight
items.statement: If π ∈ Π_alg is self-dual and some weight of π has multiplicity 1 (e.g. π regular), then π is symplectic iff w(π) is odd.

items.name: Satake parameters
items.statement: For π a level 1 cuspidal automorphic representation of PGL_n and p prime, c_p(π) is the semisimple conjugacy class in SL_n(C) attached to the unramified π_p by the Satake isomorphism.

items.name: Rankin–Selberg L-functions of level one pairs
items.statement: For π, π′ level 1 cuspidal automorphic representations of PGL_n and PGL_m, L(s, π × π′) = Π_p det(1 − p^{−s} c_p(π) ⊗ c_p(π′))^{−1} converges absolutely for Re s > 1 [JS81, JPSS83]; Λ(s, π × π′) = Γ(s, L(π_∞) ⊗ L(π′_∞)) L(s, π × π′) (2.3.1) has a meromorphic continuation to C with Λ(s, π × π′) = ε(π × π′) Λ(1 − s, π^∨ × π′^∨) (2.3.2), ε(π × π′) ∈ C^× independent of s; for π, π′ algebraic ε(π × π′) = ε(L(π_∞) ⊗ L(π′_∞)) (2.3.3). Λ(s, π × π′) is entire unless π′ ≃ π^∨, in which case its only poles are simple, at s = 0, 1 [MW89, App.].
items.note: AL.3 plans the GL_n × GL_m integrals, the global unfolding for cuspidal data, the functional equation and the poles in the contragredient case (JPSS83 is its source). Boundedness in vertical strips is item rankin-selberg-vertical-strips.

items.name: Boundedness in vertical strips
items.statement: Λ(s, π × π′) is bounded in vertical strips away from its poles [GS01].
items.note: Gelbart–Shahidi; AL.3 plans archimedean vertical-strip statements, not the global boundedness.

items.name: Weil's explicit formula (Mestre's formalism)
items.statement: Let A, B > 0, a_i, a′_i ≥ 0 (1 ≤ i ≤ M) with Σ a_i = Σ a′_i, b_i, b′_i ∈ C with non-negative real parts, and Λ_1, Λ_2 meromorphic on C with (i) Λ_1(1 − s) = wΛ_2(s) for some w ∈ C^×; (ii) finitely many poles; (iii) Λ_i minus its singular parts bounded in every vertical strip of finite width; (iv) for some c ≥ 0 and Re s > 1 + c, Λ_1(s) = A^s Π_{i=1}^M Γ(a_i s + b_i) Π_p Π_{i=1}^{M′} (1 − α_i(p)p^{−s})^{−1} and Λ_2(s) = B^s Π_{i=1}^M Γ(a′_i s + b′_i) Π_p Π_{i=1}^{M′} (1 − β_i(p)p^{−s})^{−1} with |α_i(p)|, |β_i(p)| ≤ p^c. Let F: R → R be such that, for some ε > 0, F(x) exp((1/2 + c + ε)x) is integrable and of bounded variation (with F(x) the mean of its one-sided limits), and (F(x) − F(0))/x is of bounded variation. Then Σ_ρ Φ(ρ) − Σ_μ Φ(μ) + Σ_{i=1}^M I(a_i, b_i) + Σ_{i=1}^M J(a′_i, b′_i) = F(0) log(AB) − Σ_{p,i,k≥1} (α_i(p)^k F(k log p) + β_i(p)^k F(−k log p)) log p / p^{k/2}, where ρ (resp. μ) runs over the zeros (resp. poles) of Λ_1 with −c ≤ Re ≤ 1 + c, with multiplicity, Σ_ρ Φ(ρ) = lim_{T→∞} Σ_{|Im ρ|<T} Φ(ρ), Φ(s) = ∫_R F(x) e^{(s−1/2)x} dx, I(a, b) = a ∫_0^∞ (F(ax) e^{−(a/2+b)x}/(1 − e^{−x}) − F(0) e^{−x}/x) dx and J(a, b) is the same with F(−ax).
items.note: Read in [Mes86] (Numdam, §§I.1–I.2, pp. 210–213). The paper applies it with c = 0 to Λ(s, π^∨ × π′) (item explicit-formula-RS) and says one may simply take F compactly supported of class C². AN.3 plans explicit formulas with test-function hypotheses (source KED-ANT), not Mestre's general form. Mathlib's Fourier transform has the paper's convention F̂(ξ) = ∫ F(x) e^{−2iπxξ} dx on R; F̂ at complex points needs its continuation.

items.name: The bilinear forms B_f, B_∞, Z, δ, e⊥
items.statement: For a test function F, the symmetric bilinear forms on RΠ_alg: (a) B_f^F(π, π′) = Σ_{p,k≥1} F(k log p) (log p / p^{k/2}) tr(c_p(π)^k) tr(c_p(π′)^k); (b) B_∞^F(π, π′) = J_F(L(π_∞) ⊗ L(π′_∞)) with J_F(U) = −∫_R Re (Γ′/Γ)(1/2 + 2πit, U) F(t) dt (2.3.4), also viewed on K_∞ by B_∞^F(U, V) = J_F(U·V); (c) Z^F(π, π′) = lim_{T→∞} Σ_ρ ord_{s=ρ} Λ(s, π^∨ × π′) F̂((1 − 2ρ)/4iπ), over zeros with |Im ρ| ≤ T and 0 ≤ Re ρ ≤ 1; (d) δ(π, π′) = 1 if π ≃ π′, 0 otherwise; (e) e⊥(π, π′) = 1 if π, π′ are self-dual with ε(π × π′) = −1, 0 otherwise.

items.name: The explicit formula on RΠ_alg (2.3.5)
items.statement: For every test function F, B_f^F + B_∞^F + ½ Z^F = F̂(i/4π) δ as bilinear forms on RΠ_alg.

items.name: The form C^F and condition (POS)
items.statement: C^F := F̂(i/4π) δ − B_∞^F − ½ F̂(0) e⊥ (2.3.6), the computable part of the explicit formula. A test function F satisfies (POS) if F(x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ R and F̂(ξ) ≥ 0 for all ξ ∈ C with |Im ξ| ≤ 1/4π (Definition 2.1). F̂(0) and F̂(i/4π) are real, and non-negative if F ≥ 0.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (positivity)
items.statement: Let F be a test function satisfying (POS). Then for every r ≥ 1, π_1, …, π_r ∈ Π_alg and real t_1, …, t_r ≥ 0, C^F(Σ t_i π_i, Σ t_i π_i) ≥ 0 (2.3.7).
items.note: Proof: C^F = B_f^F + ½(Z^F − F̂(0) e⊥); B_f^F is positive semidefinite as F ≥ 0, and Z^F(π, π′) ≥ F̂(0) e⊥(π, π′) since e⊥ = 1 forces a zero at s = 1/2. For integral t_i this is [CL19, Cor. 9.3.12].

items.name: Corollary 2.3 (the basic inequalities)
items.statement: Let F satisfy (POS) and U ∈ K_∞. If some π ∈ Π_alg has L(π_∞) = U, then B_∞^F(U, U) ≤ F̂(i/4π) (2.4.1). If there are distinct π_1, …, π_m ∈ Π_alg with L((π_j)_∞) = U for all j, then B_∞^F(U, U) ≤ F̂(i/4π)/m (2.4.2).
items.note: Footnote 7: in fact e⊥(x, x) = 0 here, since ε(π × π′) = 1 when L(π_∞) = L(π′_∞) ([Art13, Thm. 1.5.3(b)], or ε(U·U) = 1 directly). (2.4.2) is an effective Harish-Chandra finiteness theorem.

items.name: Miller's vanishing theorem
items.statement: For n ≤ 12 there is no π ∈ Π_alg ∖ {1} such that L(π_∞) is I_1 + I_3 + ⋯ + I_{2n+1} or ε_{C/R}^n + I_2 + I_4 + ⋯ + I_2n.
items.note: The Rankin–Selberg explicit formula (2.4.1) applied by Miller. PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 records the same theorem (as the vanishing of H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C) for 1 < n < 27) in its proposed Part II LevelOneCuspidalCohomologyGLn; one owner should hold it (see the report).

items.name: Positive definiteness of B_∞ in low weight
items.statement: For every integer 0 ≤ w ≤ 23 there is ℓ > 0 such that the restriction of B_∞^{F_ℓ} to K_∞^{≤w} is positive definite (e.g. ℓ = 4.38 for w = 22 and ℓ = 9.74 for w = 23). Hence for c > 0 there are finitely many effective U ∈ K_∞^{≤w} with B_∞^{F_ℓ}(U, U) ≤ c, and whenever U ∈ K_∞^{≤w} lies outside an explicit finite list there is no π ∈ Π_alg with L(π_∞) = U.
items.locator: Section 2.4.1, p. 278; Remark 2.11, p. 281; Section 2.4.6, p. 284; Section 4.1, p. 295
items.note: Cited from [CL19, Lemma 9.3.37, Prop. 9.3.40] and [Chea].

items.name: The quadruples Q, the forms β_Q^F and Problem 2
items.statement: A quadruple Q = (r, U, δ, m) consists of r ≥ 1, U = (U_i) ∈ K_∞^r, δ = (δ_i) ∈ {0, 1}^r and m = (m_i) ∈ Z_{≥1}^r (2.4.3). On R^r with its standard scalar product and basis (e_i), β_Q^F(e_i, e_j) = (1/m_i) F̂(i/4π) e_i·e_j − J_F(U_i·U_j) − F̂(0) δ_i δ_j (1 − ε(U_i·U_j))/4 (2.4.4). S_+^{r−1} = {t ∈ R^r : Σ t_i² = 1, t_i ≥ 0}; μ_Q^F is the minimum of β_Q^F(x, x) on D = S_+^{r−1}; for ∅ ≠ I ⊂ {1, …, r}, E_I = ⊕_{i∈I} R e_i, D_I = D ∩ E_I, D̊_I its interior, λ_I the least eigenvalue of (β_Q^F(e_i, e_j))_{i,j∈I} and E_{I,λ_I} its eigenspace. Problem 2: decide whether x ↦ β_Q^F(x, x) takes a negative value on S_+^{r−1}.
items.note: The normalisation 1/m_i in (2.4.4) is the one implemented in the authors' code; it does not match the 1/√m weights used later (source issue E3).

items.name: From Question 2.4 to Problem 2
items.statement: Let Q = (r, U, δ, m) with all m_i = 1. If there are distinct π_1, …, π_r ∈ Π_alg with L((π_i)_∞) = U_i and sd(π_i) = δ_i, then ι: e_i ↦ π_i is an isometry onto V = ⊕ R π_i with C^F(ι(x), ι(y)) = β_Q^F(x, y), using B_∞^F(π_i, π_j) = J_F(U_i·U_j) and e⊥(π_i, π_j) = δ_i δ_j (1 − ε(U_i·U_j))/2 (2.4.5). Hence if β_Q^F(t, t) < 0 for some t ∈ S_+^{r−1} (F satisfying (POS)), no such π_i exist.

items.name: Proposition 2.5
items.statement: Fix F and Q. Let 𝓘 be the set of non-empty I ⊂ {1, …, r} such that E_{I,λ_I} meets D̊_I. Then 𝓘 ≠ ∅ and μ_Q^F = min_{I ∈ 𝓘} λ_I.

items.name: Lemma 2.6
items.statement: Let E be a Euclidean space with unit sphere S, b a symmetric bilinear form on E and u the symmetric endomorphism with b(x, y) = x·u(y). If x ↦ b(x, x) restricted to S has a local minimum at v ∈ S, then v is an eigenvector of u whose eigenvalue b(v, v) is the least eigenvalue of u.
items.note: Mathlib (Rayleigh.lean:267, :296 at 082e2d3) gives: a local extremum of the Rayleigh quotient on a sphere is an eigenvector; a global minimum has the least eigenvalue. The step 'a local minimum on the sphere is global' (the second half of the paper's proof) is not in Mathlib.

items.name: Example 2.7
items.statement: If r = 2 and (β_Q^F(e_i, e_j)) = (a b; b c) with a, c ≥ 0, then μ_Q^F < 0 iff ac < b² and b < 0, i.e. iff b + √(ac) < 0.

items.name: Lemma 2.8
items.statement: Fix F and Q with μ_Q^F < 0 and F̂(i/4π) > 0, and suppose (U_i, δ_i, m_i) = (U_j, δ_j, m_j) for some i ≠ j. Then every t ∈ D with β_Q^F(t, t) = μ_Q^F has t_i = t_j.
items.note: Proof via (2.4.6): q(s_i e_i + s_j e_j + Σ_{l≠i,j} t_l e_l) = −(2/m_i) s_i s_j F̂(i/4π) + (a function of s_i + s_j), which is consistent with (2.4.4) as printed.

items.name: Corollary 2.9 (merging equal parameters), corrected normalisation
items.statement: Let Q = (r, U, δ, m) with all m_i = 1, {1, …, r} = ∐_{l=1}^{r′} P_l with (U_i, δ_i) constant on each P_l, and Q′ = (r′, U′, δ′, m′) with m′_l = |P_l|. For F with F̂(i/4π) > 0: μ_Q^F < 0 iff μ_{Q′}^F < 0. With β as in (2.4.4), ρ′: e_l ↦ (1/m′_l) Σ_{i∈P_l} e_i satisfies β_Q^F(ρ′x, ρ′y) = β_{Q′}^F(x, y); the isometry ρ: e_l ↦ (1/√m′_l) Σ_{i∈P_l} e_i satisfies β_Q^F(ρx, ρy) = β_{Q′}^F(Dx, Dy) with D = diag(√m′_l), so μ_Q^F and μ_{Q′}^F need not be equal. (They are equal, as the paper states, if (2.4.4) is replaced by F̂(i/4π) e_i·e_j − √(m_i m_j) (J_F(U_i·U_j) + F̂(0) δ_i δ_j (1 − ε(U_i·U_j))/4).)
items.locator: Section 2.4.2, the paragraph before Corollary 2.9 and Corollary 2.9, pp. 280–281
items.note: Corrected statement (source issue E3): as printed, the paper asserts β_Q(ρ(x), ρ(y)) = β_{Q′}(x, y) and μ_{Q′} = μ_Q, which fail with (2.4.4) (one block of size 2 gives μ_Q = 2μ_{Q′}). The sign equivalence, which is all that is used, holds.

items.name: Remark 2.10 (monotonicity in δ)
items.statement: If Q = (r, U, δ, m) and Q′ = (r, U, δ′, m) with δ′_i ≥ δ_i for all i, and F̂(0) ≥ 0, then β_{Q′}^F(x, y) ≤ β_Q^F(x, y) for all x, y ∈ R_{≥0}^r; hence μ_{Q′}^F ≤ μ_Q^F, and μ_Q^F < 0 implies μ_{Q′}^F < 0.

items.name: Odlyzko's test functions F_ℓ
items.statement: For ℓ > 0, F_ℓ(x) = g(x/ℓ)/cosh(x/2), where g(t) = (1 − |t|) cos(πt) + sin(π|t|)/π for |t| ≤ 1 and 0 otherwise (twice the convolution square of x ↦ cos(πx) 1_{|x|≤1/2}). F_ℓ satisfies (POS), F̂_ℓ(i/4π) = 8ℓ/π², and F̂_ℓ(0), J_{F_ℓ}(1) and J_{F_ℓ}(I_w) have closed formulas in special values of ψ = Γ′/Γ and ψ′ plus rapidly converging series with explicit tail bounds [CL19, Prop. 9.3.18 and (3) p. 277].
items.note: The closed form of g is from the authors' code (without_GRH.gp); the paper defines g by the convolution. The worker's port of those formulas reproduces the authors' certificate values to 6 digits. Mathlib defines the digamma function (Digamma.lean:48) but not ψ′ special values or these integrals.

items.name: Certified evaluation of the explicit-formula quantities
items.statement: Certified intervals for F̂_ℓ(0), F̂_ℓ(i/4π) and J_{F_ℓ}(U) for U = 1 and U = I_w (w ∈ Z), from the closed formulas of [CL19, Prop. 9.3.18] and their tail estimates, using only the four operations, exp, log, π, ψ and ψ′ in ball arithmetic (Arb, through Sage); similarly for G_ℓ with Proposition 4.4.
items.note: Implementation in the authors' sage/verify.sage. Routed to ComputationalNumberTheory CN.4.

items.name: Exact enumeration of short effective vectors (Remark 2.11)
items.statement: For 0 ≤ w ≤ 23, ℓ with B_∞^{F_ℓ} positive definite on K_∞^{≤w}, and c > 0: enumerate all effective U ∈ K_∞^{≤w} with B_∞^{F_ℓ}(U, U) ≤ c, using certified rational lower bounds (in 10^{−6}Z) for the Gram matrix and the first Fincke–Pohst algorithm [FP85] in exact arithmetic, with the effectivity condition built into the recursion.
items.note: The authors' liste_qfminim (qfminim_trie.gp) enlarges the bound by a factor 1.001, so its lists contain the required sets (source issue E4).

items.name: Algorithm 2.4.4
items.statement: Input Q = (r, U, δ, m). Step 1: choose ℓ > 0 and approximate the Gram matrix of β_Q^{F_ℓ}. Step 2: choose ∅ ≠ I ⊂ {1, …, r} and approximate λ_I and an eigenvector (t_i)_{i∈I} (PARI qfjacobi). Step 3: if λ_I < 0 and all t_i > 0 return (ℓ, I, t), else change I, then ℓ. Step 4: check β_Q^{F_ℓ}(t, t) < 0 rigorously with interval arithmetic. Only the final check is part of a proof; the output (ℓ, I, t) is a certificate that can be re-checked instantly.
items.note: In the applications ℓ ∈ [1/2, 15] ∩ 10^{−2}Z; subsets I are tried by increasing size.

items.name: Algorithm 2.4.5, corrected output
items.statement: Fix U ∈ K_∞, δ ∈ {0, 1}, m ≥ 1 and a known set S ⊂ Π_alg (with L(ϖ_∞) and sd(ϖ) given for ϖ ∈ S), and let 𝒮 be the set of triples (U′, δ′, m′) with exactly m′ elements ϖ ∈ S having (L(ϖ_∞), sd(ϖ)) = (U′, δ′). With r = 1 + |𝒮|, (U_1, δ_1, m_1) = (U, δ, m) and 𝒮 = {(U_i, δ_i, m_i) : 2 ≤ i ≤ r}, apply Algorithm 2.4.4 to Q = (r, U, δ, m) with subsets I ∋ 1. If it returns (ℓ, I, t) with β_Q^{F_ℓ}(t, t) < 0, then there are no distinct π_1, …, π_m ∈ Π_alg ∖ S with L((π_i)_∞) = U and sd(π_i) ≥ δ: otherwise x = (t_1/m)(π_1 + ⋯ + π_m) + Σ_{i=2}^r (t_i/m_i) Σ_{ϖ ↦ i} ϖ satisfies C^{F_ℓ}(x, x) ≤ β_Q^{F_ℓ}(t, t) < 0 (by Remark 2.10), contradicting Proposition 2.2. For S = ∅ this is Corollary 2.3; for |𝒮| = 1 it is [CL19, Scholium 9.3.26] (Example 2.7).
items.note: Corrected statement (source issue E3): the paper uses the weights 1/√m and 1/√m_j (and indexes j = 2, …, m for j = 2, …, r); with (2.4.4) as printed the correct weights are 1/m and 1/m_j. Footnote 10: no non-self-dual element of Π_alg is known.

items.name: New proof of the classification in motivic weight 22 (Section 2.4.6)
items.statement: The only π ∈ Π_alg of motivic weight 22 is Sym²Δ_11 (L(π_∞) = I_22 + ε_{C/R}). Proof: (1) B_∞^{F_ℓ} is positive definite on K_∞^{≤22} for ℓ = 4.38, and the effective U ∈ K_∞^{≤22} with B_∞^{F_ℓ}(U, U) ≤ F̂_ℓ(i/4π), det U = 1 and I_22 ⊂ U form a list 𝒰 of 158 elements; (2) N(U) ≤ 1 for U ∉ 𝒰′ = {I_22 + I_12, I_22 + I_10, I_22 + I_8} and N(U) ≤ 2 on 𝒰′ by (2.4.2); (3) Algorithm 2.4.5 with δ = 0, m = 2 and S = {1, Δ_11, Δ_15, Δ_17, Δ_19, Δ_21, Sym²Δ_11} (adding Δ_{21,9} for I_22 + I_8) gives N(U) ≤ 1 on 𝒰′; (4) Algorithm 2.4.5 with δ = m = 1 and ℓ ∈ [3, 5] ∩ ¼Z excludes every U ∈ 𝒰, seven of them (Table 1) needing subsets S′ of size 2.
items.note: Reproves [CL19, Thm. 9.3.3] without Satake parameters. The C-values printed for the displayed elements x are the values β_Q(t, t) of the certificates, i.e. those of the elements with weight t_1/2 on π_1 + π_2 (source issue E3; the worker reproduced −0.173, −0.198, −0.147).

items.name: No self-dual π with L(π_∞) = 2I_w (Section 2.4.7)
items.statement: For every odd 1 ≤ w ≤ 53 there is no self-dual π ∈ Π_alg (on PGL_4) with L(π_∞) = I_w + I_w.
items.note: Algorithm 2.4.5 with U = 2I_w, δ = m = 1, S the representations generated by level-one eigenforms of weight w + 1 (|S| = 0 for w = 13 and w < 11, else 1), ℓ = 5.

items.name: Vanishing of S_{(k_1,2)}(Γ_2)
items.locator: Section 2.4.7, p. 285 ([CvdG18, Lemma A.2]); footnote 4, p. 263
items.note: From pgl4-2Iw-vanishing and [CvdG18, Lemma A.2] (Clery–van der Geer, appendix by Chenevier), which extends the known range k_1 ≤ 50.

items.name: Proposition 4.1(1)
items.statement: Let U be an effective element of K_∞^{≤23} containing I_23 with multiplicity ≥ 2 and T the set of π ∈ Π_alg with L(π_∞) = U. If |T| ≥ 2 then U = I_1 + I_7 + I_13 + I_17 + I_21 + 2I_23 and T = {π, π^∨} for some non-self-dual π.
items.note: The proof shows |T| ≥ 2 ⇒ U = I_1 + I_7 + I_13 + I_17 + I_21 + 2I_23 and |T| ≤ 2. For non-self-duality it uses that this U is not in the list V, but the authors' certificate file leaves it unresolved for δ = m = 1, so it is in V (source issue E6). The missing step (no two distinct self-dual π with this U) follows from Algorithm 2.4.5 with δ = 1, m = 2; the worker's uncertified floating-point run finds β/F̂(i/4π) ≈ −0.175 at ℓ = 7.75 with S′ = {1, Δ_21, Sym²Δ_11, Δ_{23,7}}.

items.name: Proposition 4.1(2)
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 4.1(1), if T = {π} then U belongs to an explicit set V of 181 elements and π is of symplectic type.
items.note: Every U ∈ V contains I_23 at least twice, some I_w (w ∈ {1, 3, 5}) and each I_w (w ≤ 9 odd) at most once, so U has a component of multiplicity one and no invariant symmetric pairing ([Art13, Thm. 1.4.2]). The remark 'They all satisfy 14 ≤ dim U ≤ 42' is wrong: the dimensions range from 10 to 38 (source issue E7).

items.name: Lemma 4.3
items.statement: Let n ≥ 13 and π a self-dual level 1 cuspidal algebraic regular automorphic representation of PGL_n over Q of motivic weight 24. Then L(π_∞) is 1 + I_6 + I_8 + I_14 + I_20 + I_22 + I_24 or 1 + I_6 + I_10 + I_16 + I_20 + I_22 + I_24 (n = 13), or I_2 + I_4 + I_12 + I_14 + I_18 + I_20 + I_22 + I_24 or I_2 + I_8 + I_12 + I_14 + I_18 + I_20 + I_22 + I_24 (n = 16). In particular n ≤ 16.
items.note: Proof: π is orthogonal, so ε(L(π_∞)) = ε(π) = 1 ([Art13, Thm. 1.5.3]); the 1260 multiplicity-free effective U ∈ K_∞^{≤24} containing I_24 with dim U > 12, det U = 1, ε(U) = 1 (count reproduced by the worker) are tested by Algorithm 2.4.5 with δ = m = 1 against the known elements of motivic weight ≤ 23 and dimension ≤ 4 (16 representations, 15 triples; printed '15 elements', source issue E10), ℓ ∈ [3, 7] ∩ ½Z, |S′| ≤ 7.

items.name: The hypothesis (GRH) for Π_alg
items.statement: (GRH): for all π, π′ ∈ Π_alg, the zeros s ∈ C of Λ(s, π × π′) satisfy Re s = 1/2.
items.note: A conditional hypothesis for the statement register of AnalyticNumberTheory AN.6.

items.name: Positivity under GRH
items.statement: Assume (GRH). Then Proposition 2.2 holds for every test function F with F(x) ≥ 0 and F̂(ξ) ≥ 0 for all real x, ξ; in particular for G_ℓ(x) = g(x/ℓ), ℓ > 0 (Odlyzko's functions under GRH).

items.name: Proposition 4.4
items.statement: Let ℓ > 0, φ(z) = ½ψ((z+1)/2) − ½ψ(z/2) and r(z) = 2π² e^{−z}/(z² + π²)². For every integer w ≥ 0, with b = (1 + w)/2: J_{G_ℓ}(I_w) = log 2π − Re ψ(b + iπ/ℓ) + (1/π) Im ψ(b + iπ/ℓ) − (1/ℓ) Re ψ′(b + iπ/ℓ) + s_1(b, ℓ), s_1(b, ℓ) = ℓ Σ_{n≥0} r(ℓ(b + n)); J_{G_ℓ}(1 − ε_{C/R}) = Re φ(1/2 + iπ/ℓ) − (1/π) Im φ(1/2 + iπ/ℓ) + (1/ℓ) Re φ′(1/2 + iπ/ℓ) + s_2(ℓ), s_2(ℓ) = ℓ Σ_{n≥0} (−1)^n r(ℓ(n + 1/2)); Ĝ_ℓ(0) = 8ℓ/π²; and Ĝ_ℓ(i/4π) = 4π²ℓ (1 + cosh(ℓ/2))/(ℓ²/4 + π²)².
items.note: Proof follows [CL19, Prop. 9.3.18] ('straightforward details omitted'), with S(b, ℓ) and h(α) as in the paper; tail bounds from [CL19, (3) p. 277].

items.name: The certificate lists
items.statement: The stored certificates (ℓ, S′, t) of the computations: 158 + 3 for motivic weight 22 (Section 2.4.6), the δ = 0, m = 2 list for U_2 and the 12106 triples for motivic weight 23 with m = 1 (Section 4.1), the 1256 triples of Lemma 4.3, the GRH list for Theorem 4, the sets Λ of Section 3.3 with their (P1′) certificates, and the tables of masses [CT19b].
items.note: Published by the authors (levelone_src_data.tar.gz). Checked by the worker: file counts (12293 = 12106 + 187 for weight 23 with m = 1; 3 and 158 for weight 22), and 7 certificate values recomputed from a port of their formulas. Routed to ComputationalNumberTheory CN.5.

items.name: The set Π_disc(Sp_2g)
items.statement: Π_disc(Sp_2g) is the set of isomorphism classes of discrete automorphic representations π of Sp_2g over Q with π_p^{Sp_2g(Z_p)} ≠ 0 for every prime p. For π ∈ Π_disc(Sp_2g), c(π_p) is its Satake parameter in SO_{2g+1}(C) and c(π_∞) its infinitesimal character in Lie SO_{2g+1}(C).

items.name: Level 1 global Arthur parameters
items.statement: Ψ(Sp_2g) is the set of finite collections ψ of distinct triples (π_i, n_i, d_i), i ∈ I, with n_i, d_i ≥ 1, 2g + 1 = Σ n_i d_i, and π_i a level 1 self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of PGL_{n_i} over Q, orthogonal if d_i is odd and symplectic otherwise; ψ is viewed as the isobaric representation ⊞_i ⊞_{0≤r_i≤d_i−1} π_i |·|^{(d_i−1)/2 − r_i} of GL_{2g+1} (5.1.1), written ψ = ⊕ π_i[d_i], with Satake parameters ψ_p and infinitesimal character ψ_∞. ψ is algebraic if the eigenvalues of ψ_∞ are integers (then all π_i are algebraic), and then ψ_R: W_R × SL_2(C) → SO_{2g+1}(C) is defined up to conjugacy by St ∘ ψ_R ≃ ⊕_i L((π_i)_∞) ⊗ Sym^{d_i−1} C²; ψ_R is trivial on R_{>0} × 1. Ψ(SO_n) is defined in the same way with Σ n_i d_i = n.
items.note: ML.4 owns Arthur's parameters in general; this is their level-one form ([Taï17, §4], [CL19, Ch. 8]).

items.name: Arthur's standard parameter
items.statement: Every π ∈ Π_disc(Sp_2g) has a unique ψ(π) ∈ Ψ(Sp_2g) with ψ(π)_v = St ∘ c(π_v) for every place v of Q.

items.name: Root numbers of pairs of the same type
items.statement: If π_i and π_j are self-dual cuspidal, both orthogonal or both symplectic, then ε(π_i × π_j) = 1; in particular ε(π) = 1 for π orthogonal.
items.locator: Section 5.1, p. 301; footnote 7; Section 4.2, p. 298 ([Art13, Thm. 1.5.3])

items.name: The group C_ψ and Arthur's character ε_ψ at level one
items.statement: For ψ = ⊕_{i∈I} π_i[d_i] ∈ Ψ(Sp_2g) algebraic, write I = I_even ∐ I_odd according to the parity of n_i d_i. C_ψ is the elementary abelian 2-group generated by s_i (i ∈ I_even) and s_ij (i, j ∈ I_odd), with 1 = s_i² = s_ij² and s_ij s_jk = s_ik; it has order 2^{|I|−1}. With ε(i) = Π_{j≠i} ε(π_i × π_j)^{min(d_i, d_j)} (5.1.2), Arthur's character is ε_ψ(s_i) = ε(i) (i ∈ I_even) and ε_ψ(s_ij) = ε(i)ε(j) (i, j ∈ I_odd) (5.1.3).
items.note: The explicit level-one form of Arthur's ε_ψ (the adjoint of SO_{2g+1}(C) is Λ² St).

items.name: Archimedean Arthur packets and their characters
items.statement: Arthur attaches to ψ_R a finite multiset Π(ψ_R) of unitary irreducible (g, K)-modules with π_∞ ∈ Π(ψ(π)_R) for all π ∈ Π_disc(Sp_2g), and a map Π(ψ_R) → Hom(C_{ψ_R}, {±1}), U ↦ χ_U, where C_{ψ_R} is the centraliser of the image of ψ_R; the map depends on a Whittaker datum for Sp_2g(R) (fixed globally, unramified at every p, Remark 5.1). There is a natural embedding ι: C_ψ → C_{ψ_R}.

items.name: Arthur's multiplicity formula at level one
items.statement: Let ψ ∈ Ψ(Sp_2g) be algebraic and U ∈ Π(ψ_R) of multiplicity one in Π(ψ_R). There is π ∈ Π_disc(Sp_2g) with ψ(π) = ψ and π_∞ ≃ U iff ε_ψ(s_i) = χ_U(ι(s_i)) for all i ∈ I_even and ε_ψ(s_ij) = χ_U(ι(s_ij)) for all i, j ∈ I_odd (5.1.4); then π has multiplicity 1 in the discrete spectrum. The condition holds trivially when ψ = π[d] (Remark 5.2).
items.note: [Art13, Thm. 1.5.2]; the multiplicity-one hypothesis on U holds in the paper's cases by [AMR18] and [MR].

items.name: Holomorphic lowest weight modules ρ_k
items.statement: For k = (k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g ≥ 0) ∈ Z^g, ρ_k is the holomorphic unitary lowest weight (g, K)-module of lowest weight k of Sp_2g(R); it exists iff k_g ≥ g − (u + v/2) with u = |{i : k_i = k_g}| and v = |{i : k_i = k_g + 1}|, and is then unique (Enright–Howe–Wallach). The eigenvalues of its infinitesimal character are 0 and ±(k_i − i), 1 ≤ i ≤ g; they are distinct iff k_g > g, which is exactly when ρ_k is a (holomorphic) discrete series. In the scalar case k = (k, …, k) it is written ρ_k(g).
items.note: Enright–Howe–Wallach is cited in footnote 15 without a bibliography entry.

items.name: Siegel eigenforms and Π_disc(Sp_2g)
items.statement: A Hecke eigenform F ∈ L²_k(Γ_g) generates π(F) ∈ Π_disc(Sp_2g) with π(F)_∞ ≃ ρ_k; dim L²_k(Γ_g) (resp. dim S_k(Γ_g)) is the number of π ∈ Π_disc(Sp_2g) with π_∞ ≃ ρ_k counted with their discrete (resp. cuspidal) multiplicity. ψ(π(F)) is algebraic and ρ_k ∈ Π(ψ(π(F))_R).

items.name: S_k = L²_k when k_g > g
items.statement: If k_g > g, then S_k(Γ_g) = L²_k(Γ_g) (Wallach).
items.note: Cited ('a general result of Wallach'); no reference given.

items.name: Key fact 1, precise form (Section 5.2.1)
items.statement: Let ψ = ⊕_{i∈I} π_i[d_i] ∈ Ψ(Sp_2g) have ψ_∞ with eigenvalues 0 and ±(k_i − i), k_g > g. Then I_odd = {i_0}, every π_i is regular (so n_i d_i ≡ 0 mod 4 for i ≠ i_0), ψ_R is an Adams–Johnson parameter and Π(ψ_R) is the Adams–Johnson packet (each element of multiplicity one) [AMR18]; ρ_k ∈ Π(ψ_R) iff d_{i_0} = 1, and then for i ∈ I_even, χ_{ρ_k}(ι(s_i)) = (−1)^{n_i d_i/4} if d_i is even and (−1)^{e_i} otherwise, e_i being the number of odd 1 ≤ j ≤ g such that k_j − j is a weight of π_i (5.2.1). The sign does not depend on the Whittaker datum.

items.name: Adams–Johnson packets are Arthur packets
items.statement: For ψ_R an Adams–Johnson parameter (regular algebraic case), Arthur's packet Π(ψ_R) coincides with the packet Adams and Johnson attach to ψ_R [AJ87], each element with multiplicity one, and the map U ↦ χ_U has the expected form [AMR18].
items.note: Arancibia–Moeglin–Renard; a statement about Arthur packets of real classical groups, routed to ML.4.

items.name: Moeglin–Renard: packets containing ρ_k(g)
items.statement: For g ≥ k ≥ 1 and ψ with ψ_∞ having eigenvalues 0 and ±(k − i), 1 ≤ i ≤ g: ρ_k(g) ∈ Π(ψ_R) iff ψ is in case (I) or (H) of [MR, Thm. 7.1]; then ρ_k(g) has multiplicity one in Π(ψ_R), and χ_{ρ_k(g)} is given by [MR, Prop. 18.3] in terms of a sign δ representing the class of the Whittaker datum.
items.note: Moeglin–Renard, Nagoya Math. J. (2019); their n, m, π_n(m)* are the paper's g, k, ρ_k(g).

items.name: Definition 5.3: condition (R_k)
items.statement: For k, n ≥ 1 and π a cuspidal algebraic automorphic representation of PGL_n, r(π) is the multiplicity of the weight 0 of π; π satisfies (R_k) if (i) its weights are ≤ k − 1, (ii) its non-zero weights have multiplicity 1, and (iii) r(π) ≤ 3 and each of 1 and ε_{C/R} has multiplicity at most 2 in L(π_∞).
items.note: Definition 5.3 is new in the published version; arXiv v1 numbers the later statements of §5 one lower.

items.name: Case (I) and formula (5.2.3)
items.statement: In case (I) ([MR, Thm. 7.1(i)]): I_0 = {i_0}, the weight 0 of π_{i_0} has multiplicity 1, d_{i_0} = d_max = 1, k − 1 > g − k, the g integers w + (d_i − 1)/2 − r_i (w a positive weight of π_i, 0 ≤ r_i ≤ d_i − 1) fill [k − g, k − 1], every π_i is regular with weights ≤ k − 1, C_ψ is generated by the s_i (i ≠ i_0), and χ_{ρ_k(g)}(ι(s_i)) = (−1)^{n_i d_i/4} if d_i is even and (−1)^{e_δ(π_i)} otherwise (5.2.3), where e_s(π_i) is the number of 1 ≤ j ≤ k − 1 with (−1)^j = s and k − j a weight of π_i. The sign attached to I_2w[d_i] is the product of s_j over w − (d_i−1)/2 ≤ j ≤ w + (d_i−1)/2 with s_{k−i} = δ(−1)^{i−1} (5.2.4); (5.2.3) does not depend on δ.

items.name: Case (H): the subcases (H1), (H2)
items.statement: In case (H) ([MR, Thm. 7.1(ii), 7.2]) either (H1) some i_0 ∈ I_0 has d_{i_0} = d_max = 2(g − k) + 1 and L((π_{i_0})_∞) ∋ ε_{C/R}^k, or (H2) some i_0 ∈ I_0 has d_{i_0} = d_max = 2(g − k) + 3 and L((π_{i_0})_∞) ∋ ε_{C/R}^{k−1}. With k′ = k (H1) or k − 1 (H2), ψ_R ≃ ε_{C/R}^{k′}[2(g − k′) + 1] ⊕ ψ′ with ψ′ an Adams–Johnson parameter for the compact SO(2k′), dim ψ′ = 2k′, det ψ′ = ε_{C/R}^{k′}; in case (H2), g ≤ 2k′. Every π_i satisfies (R_k) and is regular for i ≠ i_0; either π_{i_0} is regular or (H1) holds with n_{i_0} ≡ 2 mod 4 and 0 a double weight, or n_{i_0} odd, 0 a triple weight, d_{i_0} = 1, g = k. In case (H2) the weight 0 of π_{i_0} has multiplicity 1, i_0 ∈ I_odd, π_{i_0} is regular and k′ > 1 (Remark 5.4).

items.name: Case (H): the character χ_{ρ_k(g)} on C_ψ
items.note: Remark 5.5: cases (I) and (H) are disjoint for k ≠ g, case (I) is a special case of (H1) for k = g with the same formula; ψ does not always determine k (for g even, (H1) in weight g/2 equals (H2) in weight g/2 + 1).

items.name: Siegel modular forms for Γ_g = Sp_2g(Z)
items.statement: For k = (k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g) ∈ Z^g, M_k(Γ_g) is the space of vector-valued Siegel modular forms of weight k for Γ_g = Sp_2g(Z), S_k(Γ_g) ⊂ L²_k(Γ_g) ⊂ M_k(Γ_g) its subspaces of cusp forms and of square-integrable forms; in the scalar case k = (k, …, k) one writes S_k(Γ_g).
items.note: B4 defines classical forms as sections of canonical extensions with the analytic transformation-law comparison and, for Siegel data, the Hodge bundle and Schur-functor weights; B5 treats non-neat levels by descent. L²_k is not planned.

items.name: Trivial vanishing
items.statement: S_k(Γ_g) = 0 when Σ_i k_i is odd; in particular there is no non-zero Siegel modular form for Γ_g of odd scalar weight and odd genus. (Also S_k(Γ_g) = 0 for k_g < g/2, by Freitag, Resnikoff and Weissauer; not used.)
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 262; used in the proof of Lemma 5.6, p. 310

items.name: The Siegel operator
items.statement: Φ_g: M_k(Γ_g) → M_k(Γ_{g−1}) is the Siegel operator; ker Φ_g = S_k(Γ_g) (scalar weight).
items.note: AutomorphicBundles B5 plans Fourier–Jacobi expansions and cuspidality as boundary vanishing, not Φ.

items.name: Zharkovskaya's relation
items.statement: If F ∈ M_k(Γ_g) is an eigenform and Φ_g F ≠ 0, then Φ_g F is an eigenform and L(s, St, F) = L(s, St, Φ_g F) ζ(s − (g − k)) ζ(s + (g − k)).

items.name: L²_k = M_k for g ≥ 2k
items.statement: If g ≥ 2k then L²_k(Γ_g) = M_k(Γ_g) ([Wei83, Satz 3]).

items.name: Eigenforms are determined by their standard parameter
items.statement: For k scalar or k_g > g, two Hecke eigenforms in S_k(Γ_g) with the same standard parameter are proportional, so dim S_k(Γ_g) is the number of standard parameters of Hecke eigenforms in S_k(Γ_g).
items.note: From the multiplicity formula and the multiplicity-one results of [AMR18] and [MR].

items.name: Notation and the set L_24
items.statement: For v_1 > ⋯ > v_r positive odd (resp. even) integers, Δ_{v_1,…,v_r} (resp. O^e_{v_1,…,v_r}) is the unique self-dual regular π ∈ Π_alg with weights ±v_i/2 when it exists, and O^o_{v_1,…,v_r} the unique self-dual π with weights 0, ±v_i/2 (O^o_22 = Sym²Δ_11); Δ¹_23, Δ²_23 are the two representations generated by eigenforms in S_24(SL_2(Z)). L_24 ⊂ Π_alg is the set of elements of motivic weight ≤ 22, of motivic weight 23 with 23/2 of multiplicity 1, or regular self-dual of motivic weight 24; it has 11 + 13 + 3 = 27 elements, listed in the paper.

items.name: Theorem 1
items.statement: There is an explicit and implemented formula computing dim S_k(Γ_g) for any g ≤ 8 and any k with k_g > g.
items.note: Equivalent to Theorems 6 and 7 through Key fact 1 (vector-valued-packet) and Key fact 2.

items.name: The vector-valued enumeration (Section 5.3.1)
items.statement: For k = (k_1, …, k_g) with k_1 ≤ 13 and k_g > g (so 1 ≤ g ≤ 12), each π_i in the standard parameter is regular of motivic weight ≤ 24, so lies in L_24, and π_{i_0} ∈ {1, Sym²Δ_11, O^o_{24,16,8}} with d_{i_0} = 1. There are exactly 199 ψ ∈ Ψ(Sp_2g) with these properties whose ψ_∞ has distinct eigenvalues of absolute value ≤ 12, and exactly 59 of them satisfy (5.1.4) with (5.2.1), (5.1.3) and (5.1.2); they give Table 5 and the part of Table 6 with k > g.
items.note: Reproduced by the worker: 199 and 59 come out when the trivial parameter [1] (g = 0) is included and Δ¹_23, Δ²_23 are not distinguished; the 58 solutions with g ≥ 1 are the 29 rows of Table 5 and the 29 rows of Table 6 with k > g.

items.name: Theorem 2, vector-valued part (Table 5)
items.statement: For 13 ≥ k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g > g and k non-scalar, dim S_k(Γ_g) is given by Table 5: it is ≤ 1, and non-zero for exactly 29 values of k, with the standard parameters listed there.

items.name: Scalar weight, case (I)
items.statement: If k ≤ 13, g ≥ k and the standard parameter ψ of an eigenform in S_k(Γ_g) is in case (I), then ψ = Δ_11[12] ⊕ [1] (g = k = 12); this ψ satisfies (5.1.4) (ε_ψ(s_j) = ε(Δ_11) = 1 = χ_{ρ_12(12)}(ι(s_j))), and the eigenform is cuspidal by the shape of ψ and Zharkovskaya's relation.

items.name: The Ikeda lift of Δ_11
items.statement: The genus 12 Ikeda lift of Δ_11 is a non-zero element of S_12(Γ_12) with standard parameter Δ_11[12] ⊕ [1] ([Ike01]; constructed earlier in [BFW98]).

items.name: Lemma 5.6
items.statement: In case (H1) (k ≤ 13, g ≥ k), every π_i lies in L_24 and π_{i_0} = 1.
items.note: The case π_{i_0} = Sym²Δ_11 forces ψ = Sym²Δ_11[3] ⊕ Δ_11[8] ⊕ [3] ⊕ [1] (k = 13, g = 14), which fails (5.1.4) at s_i.

items.name: The parameters ψ′ in case (H1)
items.statement: In case (H1) with π_{i_0} = 1, k is even, k ≤ 12, and ψ = [2(g − k) + 1] ⊕ ψ′ with ψ′ a 2k-dimensional parameter with eigenvalues ±(k − 1), …, ±1 and 0 twice; the possible ψ′ are [2k − 1] ⊕ [1] for k = 2, 4, 6; [15] ⊕ [1] and Δ_11[4] ⊕ [7] ⊕ [1] for k = 8; five parameters for k = 10; and the 24 parameters of [CL19, Thm. E] for k = 12.
items.locator: Section 5.3.2, Case (H1), p. 311 ([CL19, Prop. 9.2.2, Thm. E])

items.name: Lemma 5.7
items.statement: In case (H1), k ≡ 0 mod 4.
items.note: For k ≡ 2 mod 4 the multiplicity formula at s_{i_1 i_2} ((5.2.9)) fails.

items.name: Level one forms for O_n and the spaces C[X_n]
items.statement: For n ≡ 0 mod 8 fix an even unimodular lattice of rank n and let O_n, SO_n be its orthogonal and special orthogonal group schemes over Z. C[X_n], with X_n the set of isometry classes of even unimodular lattices of rank n, is naturally the dual of a space of level 1 automorphic forms for O_n; a Hecke eigenform G ∈ C[X_n] generates a discrete automorphic representation π_G of O_n (trivial at ∞, with O_n(Z_p)-fixed vectors) with a standard parameter ψ_G ∈ Ψ(SO_n) ([Art13], [Taï19]).

items.name: The finite sets X_n
items.statement: For n ≡ 0 mod 8, L_n is the set of even unimodular lattices in the standard Euclidean space R^n and X_n = O(R^n)\L_n the finite set of their isometry classes.
items.note: GN.3 plans reduction domains, arithmetic quotients and mass formulas (hence finiteness of class sets). Tau Ceti's Integral lattices, discriminant forms, and overlattices has even unimodular overlattices but, by its own statement, no classification and no Niemeier or Leech lattices.

items.name: Siegel theta series
items.statement: For g ≥ 0, Siegel theta series give linear maps ϑ_g: C[X_n] → M_{n/2}(Γ_g) (5.3.1).
items.note: GN.3 plans theta-series interfaces for lattices, MP.5 the adelic theta series of a quadratic/symplectic datum; the properties used here are item theta-series-properties.

items.name: Properties of ϑ_g
items.statement: Φ ∘ ϑ_g = ϑ_{g−1}. The degree of G ∈ C[X_n] is the least g_0 ≥ 0 with ϑ_{g_0}(G) ≠ 0; ϑ_{g_0}(G) is cuspidal and ϑ_g(G) ≠ 0 for g ≥ g_0. If G is an eigenform of degree g_0 and g ≥ g_0, then ϑ_g(G) is an eigenform (Eichler commutation relations), and if F = ϑ_g(G) is square-integrable then ψ_G = ψ_F ⊕ [n − 2g_0 − 1] for n > 2g_0 + 1 and ψ_F = ψ_G ⊕ [2g_0 + 1 − n] for n < 2g_0 + 1 (Rallis).

items.name: Rallis: Satake parameters under the theta correspondence
items.statement: The relation between the Satake parameters of an eigenform on the orthogonal side and of its theta lift on the symplectic side, at unramified places ([Ral82, §6]).
items.note: The local unramified theta correspondence behind theta-series-properties; routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 (local theta modules). [Ral82] not read.

items.name: Lemma 5.8
items.statement: Let G ∈ C[X_n] be an eigenform of degree g_0. If g > g_0 and g > n − 1 − g_0, then F = ϑ_g(G) is square integrable and ψ_F = ψ_G ⊕ [2g − n + 1].
items.locator: Section 5.3.2, Lemma 5.8, p. 312 ([Ral84, Thm. I.1.1], [MW94, Lemme I.4.11], via [MR, §16.2])

items.name: Eigenforms of C[X_8], C[X_16], C[X_24] and their degrees
items.statement: dim C[X_8] = 1, dim C[X_16] = 2, dim C[X_24] = 24, and the standard parameters of their eigenforms are exactly the 1, 2 and 24 parameters ψ′ of case (H1) for k = 4, 8, 12 ([CL19, Cor. 7.2.7, Thm. E]). The degree of each eigenform is the least g_0 such that [2k − 1 − 2g_0] is a summand of ψ′ (so g_0 < k), except for ψ′ = Δ_11[12], of degree 12 ([CL19, Thm. 9.2.6]; Nebe–Venkov).

items.name: Case (H1): only the Ikeda lift is cuspidal
items.statement: In case (H1) (k ≤ 13, g ≥ k), the only standard parameter of a cuspidal eigenform is Δ_11[12] ⊕ [1] (g = k = 12): every other ψ = [2(g − k) + 1] ⊕ ψ′ is the parameter of the non-cuspidal discrete representation generated by ϑ_g of an eigenform of C[X_2k] (Lemma 5.8).

items.name: Lemma 5.9
items.statement: In case (H2) (k ≤ 13, g ≥ k): π_{i_0} = 1, k is odd and g is even.

items.name: Lemma 5.10
items.statement: In case (H2), if i ∈ I_0 and π_i ≠ 1, then π_i = Sym²Δ_11, d_i = 1, k = 13 and g = 24, and I_0 = I_odd = {i_0, i, j} with j ≠ i_0, i, π_j = 1 and d_j ≥ 5.
items.note: The remaining parameter Sym²Δ_11 ⊕ Δ_11[10] ⊕ [1] (inside ψ′) fails (5.1.4) at s_{i_0 j} by (5.2.12).

items.name: Case (H2): the forms of genus 16 and 24
items.statement: In case (H2) there are exactly two Siegel eigenforms, both of weight 13: genus 16 with parameter Δ_17[8] ⊕ [9] ⊕ [7] ⊕ [1], and genus 24 with parameter [25] ⊕ Δ_11[12]; both satisfy (5.1.4) and are cuspidal (odd weight).
items.note: The genus 24 form is Freitag's [Fre82]. The parameters Δ_21[4] ⊕ Δ_11[6] ⊕ [5] ⊕ [3] ⊕ [1] and Δ_{23,7}[2] ⊕ Δ_17[4] ⊕ Δ_11[2] ⊕ [5] ⊕ [3] ⊕ [1] fail (5.1.4) at s_h.

items.name: Theorem 2, scalar part (Table 6)
items.statement: For every k ≤ 13 and g ≥ 1, dim S_k(Γ_g) is given by Table 6. In particular S_k(Γ_g) = 0 whenever k ≤ 13 and g ≥ k, except dim S_12(Γ_12) = dim S_13(Γ_16) = dim S_13(Γ_24) = 1.
items.locator: Section 1.1, Theorem 2, p. 263; Table 6, p. 320; proof Section 5.3
items.note: The paper stresses that no previous computation of a space of Siegel modular forms, not even of S_k(SL_2(Z)), is used; it also removes the dependence of earlier vanishing results for g > k on the incorrect [Miz91, Cor. 3] (footnote 3).

items.name: Corollary 1
items.statement: S_13(Γ_g) has dimension 1 for g = 8, 12, 16, 24, and 0 otherwise.

items.name: Corollary 5.11 (Eichler's basis problem for k = 4, 8, 12)
items.statement: Assume k = 4, 8 or 12. Then ϑ_g: C[X_2k] → M_k(Γ_g) is surjective for all g; in particular Φ_g: M_k(Γ_g) → M_k(Γ_{g−1}) is surjective for all g ≥ 1.
items.note: From [CL19, §1.3] (g ≤ k ≤ 12) and S_k(Γ_g) = 0 for g > k, k ≤ 12 (Theorem 2). Not general: ϑ_20 is not surjective for k = 16 [KSM04]; [CL19, Cor. 7.3.5] for ϑ_14.

items.name: Remark 5.12
items.statement: dim M_k(Γ_g) = |X_2k| for k = 4 and g ≥ 1, for k = 8 and g ≥ 4, and for k = 12 and g ≥ 12.

items.name: Theta series with harmonic coefficients
items.statement: For U a finite-dimensional continuous representation of O(R^n), M_U(O_n) is the space of O(R^n)-equivariant functions L_n → U. For g, ν ≥ 1, H_{ν,g,n} is the representation of O(R^n) on harmonic polynomials of degree ν on M_{n,g}(C) [Bö89, §XI]; theta series with harmonic coefficients give ϑ_{ν,g,n}: M_{H_{ν,g,n}}(O_n) → S_{n/2+ν}(Γ_g) (5.4.1), sending O_n-eigenforms to Siegel eigenforms or to 0.

items.name: Böcherer's criterion
items.statement: A Siegel eigenform F_g of weight n/2 + ν lies in the image of ϑ_{ν,g,n} iff a condition on the order of vanishing of L(s, F_g, St) at s = n/2 − g holds ([Bö89, Thm. 5]).
items.note: Stated only in words in the paper; [Bö89] not read. Contributions of Siegel, Weissauer, Kudla–Rallis and others (footnote 19).

items.name: Non-vanishing of two central values
items.statement: The Godement–Jacquet L-functions of Δ_{19,7} and Δ_{21,13} do not vanish at s = 1/2.

items.name: Proposition 5.13
items.statement: Let F_g (g = 8, 12, 16, 24) be the weight 13 Siegel eigenforms of Table 6, with standard parameters Δ_{21,13}[4] ⊕ [1], Δ_{19,7}[6] ⊕ [1], Δ_17[8] ⊕ [9] ⊕ [7] ⊕ [1] and Δ_11[12] ⊕ [25]. (i) For each g, F_g is in the image of ϑ_{1,g,24}. (ii) F_8 is in the image of ϑ_{5,8,16}.
items.note: By Böcherer's criterion and a case-by-case check of L(s, F_g, St) at s = n/2 − g (details in [CT19b], verif_bocherer.pdf), using central-values-nonvanishing.

items.name: Alternating forms on the Leech lattice
items.statement: For f ∈ M_{H_{1,g,24}}(O_24) and any Niemeier lattice L, f(L) is an O(L)-invariant alternating g-form, so f vanishes outside the O(R^24)-orbit of the Leech lattice ([CT19a, Prop. 4.1]). There is a non-zero O(Leech)-invariant alternating g-form on the Leech lattice, unique up to scalar, iff g ∈ {8, 12, 16, 24}; so dim M_{H_{1,g,24}}(O_24) = 1 for g = 8, 12, 16, 24 and 0 otherwise.
items.note: The dimension count uses a character computation from the ATLAS page of O(Leech) = 2·Co_1; g = 24 follows from orientability of the Leech lattice.

items.name: Corollary 5.14
items.statement: The linear map ϑ_{1,g,24} of (5.4.1) is an isomorphism for all g ≥ 1.
items.note: Uses the main result of [CT19a] (non-vanishing of ϑ_{1,g,24} for g = 8, 12, 16, 24, via M_24 and oriented sublattices of Leech), Corollary 1 and leech-forms.

items.name: The space M_{H_{5,8,16}}(O_16)
items.statement: dim M_{H_{5,8,16}}(O_16) = 2, spanned by two O_16-eigenforms with standard parameters Δ_{21,13}[4] and Δ_17[8].
items.note: 'Using a computation similar to that of [CL19, Cor. 9.5.13]'; no details given.

items.name: Proposition 5.15
items.statement: dim M_k(Γ_g) = dim M_k(Γ_2k) whenever g ≥ 2k, and this dimension vanishes unless k is divisible by 4.
items.note: Every eigenform is in case (H1) with π_{i_0} = 1; for s = Π_{I_even} s_i (times s_{i_1 i_2}), χ(s) = (−1)^{k/2} while ε_ψ(s) = 1 by (5.5.1); the parameters ψ′ ⊕ [2(g′ − k) + 1] for g′ ≥ 2k match.

items.name: Siegel modular forms for g > 2k (5.5.2)
items.statement: For g > 2k: S_k(Γ_g) = 0 ([Res75], [Fre75]), and M_k(Γ_g) = Im ϑ_g if k ≥ 0 and k ≡ 0 mod 4, and 0 otherwise ([Fre77], see also [How81]).

items.name: Corollary 5.16(1)
items.statement: Assume g ≥ 2k. The Siegel operator Φ_{g+1}: M_k(Γ_{g+1}) → M_k(Γ_g) is bijective.

items.name: Corollary 5.16(2)
items.statement: Assume g ≥ 2k and k ≡ 0 mod 4. Then ϑ_g: C[X_2k] → M_k(Γ_g) is an isomorphism.
items.note: 'This corollary seems to be new for g = 2k.'
