routes.title: Level one automorphic forms of classical groups over Z and Siegel modular forms
routes.brief: Level one automorphic forms of the split classical groups over Z, the level one algebraic cusp forms of PGL_m over Q that parametrise them, and Siegel modular forms for Γ_g = Sp_2g(Z), following Chenevier–Taïbi, Discrete series multiplicities for classical groups over Z and level 1 algebraic cusp forms, Publ. Math. IHÉS 131 (2020) 261–323, and the book it builds on, Chenevier–Lannes, Automorphic forms and even unimodular lattices (Ergebnisse 69, 2019). Final theorems, stated as in the paper (with the corrections recorded in PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20). Theorem 1: there is an explicit and implemented formula computing dim S_k(Γ_g) for any g ≤ 8 and any k with k_g > g. Theorem 2: for 13 ≥ k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g > g and k non-scalar, dim S_k(Γ_g) is given by Table 5 (at most 1, non-zero for exactly 29 k); for every k ≤ 13 and g ≥ 1 it is given by Table 6, so S_k(Γ_g) = 0 for k ≤ 13 and g ≥ k except dim S_12(Γ_12) = dim S_13(Γ_16) = dim S_13(Γ_24) = 1. Corollary 1: S_13(Γ_g) has dimension 1 for g = 8, 12, 16, 24 and 0 otherwise. Theorem 3: exactly 13 level one cuspidal algebraic representations of PGL_m over Q have motivic weight 23 with the weight 23/2 of multiplicity 1 (two of PGL_2 from S_24(SL_2(Z)); three of PGL_4 with weights ±23/2, ±v/2, v = 7, 9, 13; seven of PGL_6 with (v, u) = (13, 5), (15, 3), (15, 7), (17, 5), (17, 9), (19, 3), (19, 11); one of PGL_10 with weights ±23/2, ±21/2, ±17/2, ±11/2, ±3/2), all symplectic and determined by their weights. Proposition 4.1: if an effective U ∈ K_∞^{≤23} contains I_23 at least twice and T is the set of π with L(π_∞) = U, then |T| ≥ 2 forces U = I_1 + I_7 + I_13 + I_17 + I_21 + 2I_23 and T = {π, π^∨} with π non-self-dual, and T = {π} forces U into an explicit list of 181 elements with π symplectic. Theorem 4 (under GRH): such a π with 23/2 of multiplicity > 1 has m = 16, weights ±1/2, ±7/2, ±11/2, ±15/2, ±19/2, ±21/2 and ±23/2 twice, and is unique. Theorem 5: exactly three self-dual regular level one algebraic cusp forms have motivic weight 24, with weights {±12, ±8, ±4, 0}, {±12, ±9, ±5, ±2} and {±12, ±10, ±7, ±1}. Theorems 6 and 7: the masses m_c of all c ∈ C(G) for G = SO_n (n ≤ 17) and Sp_2n (2n ≤ 16) are those of [CT19b]. Corollary 5.11: for k = 4, 8, 12, ϑ_g: C[X_2k] → M_k(Γ_g) is surjective for all g. Proposition 5.13 and Corollary 5.14: the four weight 13 eigenforms are Siegel theta series with harmonic coefficients, and ϑ_{1,g,24} is an isomorphism for all g ≥ 1. Proposition 5.15: dim M_k(Γ_g) = dim M_k(Γ_2k) for g ≥ 2k, zero unless 4 | k. Corollary 5.16: for g ≥ 2k the Siegel operator Φ_{g+1} is bijective, and if 4 | k then ϑ_g: C[X_2k] → M_k(Γ_g) is an isomorphism. Layers. (1) Level one algebraic cusp forms of PGL_m: Π_alg, archimedean parameters in the ring K_∞, weights and motivic weight, W_m and regularity, N(w) and N⊥(w), self-dual types, root numbers of pairs. (2) The Rankin–Selberg explicit formula on RΠ_alg and the positivity criterion: the forms B_f, B_∞, Z, δ, e⊥ and C^F, (POS), Proposition 2.2, Corollary 2.3, Miller's theorem, the quadratic problem β_Q with Propositions and Lemmas 2.5–2.10 (Corollary 2.9 and the output of Algorithm 2.4.5 in the corrected normalisation), Algorithms 2.4.4–2.4.5, Odlyzko's functions F_ℓ and, under GRH, G_ℓ (Proposition 4.4). (3) Classification in motivic weight ≤ 24: Chenevier–Lannes' theorem in weight ≤ 22 with its new proof, Theorems 3–5, Proposition 4.1 (including the δ = 1, m = 2 step the paper omits), Lemma 4.3, Section 2.4.7; every numerical step is a certificate checked through ComputationalNumberTheory CN.5. (4) Level one Arthur parameters and the explicit multiplicity formula for Sp_2g and SO_n over Z: Ψ(G), ψ_R, C_ψ and ε_ψ, the packets containing ρ_k (Key fact 1, cases (I), (H1), (H2), formulas (5.2.1)–(5.2.12)), and Key fact 2 relating EP(G; λ) to the numbers N⊥ ([Taï17, §4]). (5) Masses: EP(G; λ), w(λ), C(G), the elliptic term and masses, P(G), ∼, P_1(G) with the spinor-norm constraint, Lemmas 3.2–3.3, Corollary 3.9, Tables 2–4, the strategy (P1′)/(P2′), Theorems 6–7, Remark 3.10, the SO_3 example, and characters of V_λ at torsion elements (Weyl, Koike–Terada). (6) Siegel modular forms: ρ_k and the dictionary with Π_disc(Sp_2g), Wallach and Weissauer, the Siegel operator and Zharkovskaya's relation, Theorems 1 and 2 with Lemmas 5.6–5.10, the Ikeda lift. (7) Theta series of even unimodular lattices: level one forms on O_n, X_n and C[X_n], ϑ_g and its degree, Rallis's relation, Lemma 5.8, the eigenforms of C[X_8], C[X_16], C[X_24], harmonic theta series and Böcherer's criterion, Proposition 5.13, the Leech-lattice forms, Corollaries 5.11, 5.14, 5.16, Remark 5.12, Proposition 5.15. Imports, by title and id: Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1, AF.2, AF.4, with the existence of discrete series and the archimedean Langlands correspondence for GL_n(R) added to AF.1; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.4; Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.1 and AL.3; Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution (AnalyticNumberTheory) AN.3 and AN.6; Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions (AutomorphicSpectralTheory) AS.6, with Arthur's L²-Lefschetz formula; Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4, for Arthur's classification, the archimedean packets (with Arancibia–Moeglin–Renard and Moeglin–Renard) and the multiplicity formula; Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic) GN.2 (spinor norms over rings, Zassenhaus, Proposition 3.7) and GN.3 (genera, masses, theta interfaces); Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms) MP.3 and MP.5; Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms (AutomorphicBundles) B4–B5 for Siegel modular forms; Certified computational number theory and arithmetic data (ComputationalNumberTheory) CN.4–CN.5; and from Tau Ceti, Modular forms — Hecke theory, newforms, and L-functions (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms) with Mathlib's level-one dimension formula, Integral lattices, discriminant forms, and overlattices (tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices), Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems), Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight, Layer 6), and Clifford algebras, the Pin and Spin groups, and spin representations (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SpinRepresentations). The explicit-formula layer is the single owner of the Stark–Odlyzko method for Rankin–Selberg L-functions of Π_alg; the proposed Part II LevelOneCuspidalCohomologyGLn (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25) should import Miller's theorem from it. A statement proved by computation cites a certificate checked in exact or interval arithmetic, never a floating-point run.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas goes in this direction: no layer plans level one automorphic forms of the split classical groups over Z, the level one algebraic cusp forms of PGL_m and their classification in low motivic weight, the explicit-formula positivity method, the computation of masses in the L²-Lefschetz trace formula, or Siegel modular forms beyond their definition as sections of automorphic bundles (AutomorphicBundles B4). The paper is one step of a coherent programme (Chenevier–Lannes, Chenevier–Renard, Taïbi, Chenevier–Taïbi) whose general inputs already have owners, which the new roadmap imports. As with Lawrence–Venkatesh in the maintainer's guides, a new roadmap is the fit.

AF.1 owns the foundations of real reductive representation theory. Harish-Chandra's existence criterion for discrete series and Langlands' archimedean correspondence for GL_n(R) (as in Knapp's survey) are general statements of that kind, used here, by AL.3's archimedean factors and by ML.4's packets.

AL.1 fixes local L-, ε- and γ-factors in Tate's normalisation. The ε-factors of representations of W_R (ε(1) = 1, ε(I_w) = i^{w+1}, Tate's ε(U, ψ, dx) with ψ(x) = e^{2iπx}) are its archimedean case, needed for every root number ε(π × π′).

AL.3 owns Rankin–Selberg L-functions: continuation, functional equation, poles in the contragredient case. Gelbart–Shahidi's boundedness of Λ(s, π × π′) in vertical strips completes the analytic package the explicit formula needs.

AN.3 plans explicit formulas with test-function hypotheses. Mestre's formalism, the explicit formula for any L-function with an Euler product, functional equation, finitely many poles and bounded vertical strips, with his axioms on the test function, is the general statement; its Rankin–Selberg case on Π_alg stays in the new roadmap.
AN.6 keeps the register of RH- and GRH-type hypotheses for conditional theorems. The (GRH) of Section 4.3 for Λ(s, π × π′), π, π′ ∈ Π_alg, used by Theorem 4, is one.

AS.6 owns Arthur's invariant trace formula (from Arthur's 1988 papers, which the paper cites). Arthur's L²-Lefschetz formula [Art89], the evaluation of that formula for pseudocoefficients of discrete series with its simple geometric side, is a general theorem for reductive groups over Q; the level one mass computation only specialises it. ET.1 constructs pseudocoefficients in unitary cases only, so the general construction belongs here too.

ML.4 gives the Arthur–Mok classification inputs proof-source owners, packets included. That Adams–Johnson packets are Arthur packets with multiplicity one [AMR18], and Moeglin–Renard's description of the packets of Sp_2n(R) containing scalar unitary highest weight modules [MR], are statements about archimedean Arthur packets of real classical groups. Their level one specialisations, formulas (5.2.1)–(5.2.12), stay in the new roadmap.

GN.2 owns quadratic forms over fields and rings, with discriminants, Clifford invariants and spinor genera. The spinor norm over rings with its GSpin and Spin exact sequences, Zassenhaus's formula, Corollary 3.6 and Proposition 3.7 (characteristic polynomials of local integral isometries, after Gross–McMullen) are general quadratic-form theory, built on Tau Ceti's spinor norm over fields.

MP.3 owns local theta modules for orthogonal–symplectic dual pairs. Rallis's relation between Satake parameters under the unramified theta correspondence is a local statement of that kind; the global level one relation for Siegel theta series stays in the new roadmap.

CN.4 owns interval and ball arithmetic and validated evaluation of analytic quantities. The certified evaluation of F̂_ℓ(0), F̂_ℓ(i/4π) and J_{F_ℓ}(U) (and of J_{G_ℓ}) from digamma values and series with tail bounds, and the exact Fincke–Pohst enumeration with certified rational lower bounds, are validated numerics of that kind.

CN.5 defines certificate schemas and checks certificates in Lean. The paper's proofs by computation are certificates in this sense: the lists (ℓ, S′, t) with their interval checks, the sets Λ of Section 3.3, and the mass tables of [CT19b].
